summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation of the reduced-order beam control problem with comparative controller analysis.

papers.title: ATTUNE: Agentic Throughput Tuning for LLM Training
papers.abstract: Training recipes are tuned by hand for one model, cluster and workload, and every new model, accelerator, framework version or dataset means tuning again. Automated tuners search a fixed space of knobs and check only that a job runs, yet a configuration can run to completion while it silently changes training. ATTUNE is a single coding agent that tunes any working recipe for the workload and stack at hand, unattended, within a GPU-hour budget the user sets. It diagnoses each run and changes one lever at a time, guided by a catalog of lessons from past campaigns, and ships a recipe only if it passes a correctness gate: a configuration check against objective-changing settings and known stack defects, and a convergence check of its loss curve against the baseline's. On four held-out models at 64-128 GPUs, ATTUNE raises mean throughput over the strongest public recipe run on our stack by 6.7% on Llama-3.1-405B (best campaign 11.9%) and 33.9% on GLM-4.5 (54.7%), whose public recipe was written for H100. It keeps Mixtral-8x22B's recipe, where nothing it finds clears the noise band. Under a common GPU-hour budget it beats OptiCo, Bayesian optimization and random search on GLM-4.5 and MiniMax-M2; on GLM-4.5 its mean gain is more than four times the best alternative's at less than half the GPU-hours, and on both models its tuning pays for itself within a day of training. The gate rejects no legitimate run and catches 16 of 24 faulty runs, missing only ones that barely move the 20-step loss. Ablations tie its best campaigns to one of its search rules: retrying an out-of-memory layout with recomputation. We release ATTUNE's code and TrainingThroughputBench, a leaderboard of the fastest known recipes for MoE models up to 744B parameters on up to 256 GPUs, each with its throughput, cost per million tokens and a passed correctness check, at https://github.com/amazon-science/attune.

papers.title: CÆNL: Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning with Objective-Aligned Representation Control
papers.abstract: Active learning changes the representations used to acquire subsequent labels. We study this interaction through Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning (CÆNL), which separates acquisition, Dynamic Collapse Regularization (DCR), and its coefficient policy. DCR penalizes a normalized within-class to between-class scatter residual above a frozen reference, with a separate class-separation safeguard. Fixed, scheduled, deterministic-feedback, and learned-feedback policies apply this objective. The analysis establishes scatter invariances, conditional local descent, and coefficient bounds, and shows why clean geometry alone cannot guarantee input robustness. Six-seed classification comparisons are complemented by a 104-run study with separate control selection and ten-seed evaluations on each of two backbones. At 60% annotations on ImageNet-100, entropy acquisition with DCR and MACC-Lite reaches 73.420 +/- 0.512% accuracy on ResNet-50 and 73.086 +/- 0.397% on ResNet-18 (mean +/- seed SD), exceeding entropy alone by 1.742 and 1.834 percentage points. Both gains survive Holm correction under paired-t and exact sign-flip tests, with unchanged feedback settings across backbones. Independently tuned constants attain slightly higher mean accuracy; the paired comparisons establish neither adaptive superiority nor equivalence. Separate six-seed spectral studies yield a small fixed-regularization C4 loss reduction, worse CIFAR-10 diffusion FID, and inconclusive AudioCaps captioning effects. Earlier classification studies find near-zero AutoAttack accuracy at L-infinity radius 8/255 and no added benefit from learned control. The results support the evaluated combined classification treatment and identify the task dependence of geometry-informed regularization.

papers.title: Semantic Segmentation of Selective Laser Melting Powder Bed Images Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Hierarchical Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: Layer-wise powder bed images acquired during selective laser melting (SLM) can characterize the surface conditions after powder spreading and laser scanning, thereby providing essential information for in situ quality monitoring. Semantic segmentation enables pixel-level identification and localization of powder bed defects. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging because different defect types exhibit substantial variations in morphology and scale, while class imbalance and cross-device imaging domain shifts further complicate the task. To address the challenges of multiple defect categories, significant scale variations, imbalanced class distributions, and imaging domain shifts across different devices in powder bed image monitoring for selective laser melting (SLM), a semantic segmentation method based on multi-scale feature fusion and hierarchical transfer learning is proposed. First, post-spreading and post-scanning images from the same layer are combined to form a dual-channel input. Four parallel branches are then designed to extract global features, native-resolution details, local morphological features, and positional encodings, respectively, enabling multi-scale feature fusion to capture defect information across different spatial scales. Second, a two-stage transfer learning strategy is developed for cross-device applications. In the first stage, network parameters are updated differentially according to the domain sensitivity of individual modules. In the second stage, the entire network is jointly optimized using a small learning rate, while a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) constraint is introduced to align the feature distributions of the source- and target-domains. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 0.879. After hierarchical transfer learning, an mIoU of 0.855 is obtained on the experimental dataset from the target-domain. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the segmentation accuracy of complex powder bed defects and exhibits strong adaptability across different devices.

papers.title: Evidence Gaps in Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Registry-Based Study of Trial Discontinuation and Nonpublication From 2000 to 2024
papers.abstract: BackgroundClinical trials play a vital role in advancing evidence-based orthopedic care, yet trial discontinuation and nonpublication limit transparency and reduce the availability of clinically valuable data.In total hip arthroplasty (THA), incomplete dissemination of trial outcomes may have important ethical and clinical implications. MethodsA registry-based cross-sectional analysis of randomized Phase III and IV THA clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.govbetween 2000 and 2024 was performed.Trials registered at least two years before the search date (January 2026) were included.Trial characteristics, including funding source, intervention type, enrollment size, blinding, number of centers, and recruitment location, were extracted.Publication status was determined through registry-linked publications and independent database searches.Associations were analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests (p < 0.05). ResultsOf 168 identified trials, seven unrelated to THA were excluded, leaving 161 trials for analysis.Fifty trials (31.1%) were discontinued, and 111 (68.9%) were completed.Among completed trials, 26 (23.4%) remained unpublished.Discontinuation was significantly associated with intervention type (p = 0.0015) and blinding (p = 0.022), with higher rates in device trials (59.3%) and unblinded studies (55.9%).Nonpublication was significantly associated with industry funding (39.3% vs. 18.1%, p = 0.022) and intervention type (p = 0.044). ConclusionsA substantial proportion of THA clinical trials are discontinued or remain unpublished, contributing to data loss and potential bias in the orthopedic literature.Improved reporting compliance is needed to support transparency and evidence-based orthopedic practice.

papers.title: Computational Algorithms for Early-Age Creep and Buildability Prediction in Extrusion-Based 3D Concrete Printing: A Critical Survey
papers.abstract: Early-age deformation is a major limitation on the buildability of extrusion-based 3D-printed concrete because each deposited layer must carry increasing self-weight while hydration, thixotropic rebuilding, stiffness, and strength are still evolving. This survey reviews experimental, rheological, analytical, and numerical approaches used to characterize and predict creep and related deformation during printing. The reviewed experiments include compression, creep-recovery, digital image correlation, and full-scale printing tests. Analytical approaches include Burgers, generalized Kelvin, power-law, and hydration-coupled viscoelastic formulations, whereas numerical studies employ continuum finite elements, lattice and voxel activation, damage-rheology laws, particle finite elements, computational fluid dynamics, and coupled fluid-solid models. Across these approaches, predicted buildability depends strongly on material age at loading, load duration, deposition interval, layer geometry, and interface behavior. The literature shows that elastic models are useful for rapid screening, but viscoelastic, plastic, or damage mechanisms become important when printing duration is long or stress approaches the evolving resistance. Remaining priorities are standardized early-age tests, independent validation, uncertainty quantification, and transferable models that connect material characterization with layer-by-layer structural analysis.

papers.title: Greater three‐dimensional cam burden and superolateral location are associated with end‐stage hip osteoarthritis: A retrospective comparative study
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Cam‐type femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is a recognised structural contributor to primary hip osteoarthritis (OA), yet many cam‐positive hips do not progress to radiographic joint failure. This study aimed to compare three‐dimensional cam morphology and lesion location between cam‐positive hips with end‐stage primary osteoarthritis and cam‐positive, non‐arthritic hips in an elderly fracture cohort. Methods Hospital records and imaging archives from January 2020 to January 2026 were retrospectively reviewed at a single centre. The OA group comprised patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for primary OA, and the fracture group comprised patients aged ≥ 65 years treated for intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric femoral fractures without radiographic OA. Cam morphology was characterised using radial CT‐based alpha angle, three‐dimensional cam volume, cam/head volume ratio, and clock‐face–based lesion location. Group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic analyses, correlation testing, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results A total of 438 cam‐positive hips were included (126 OA and 312 fracture). OA hips demonstrated higher alpha angles (72.44° ± 5.94° vs. 62.45° ± 5.07°), larger cam volumes (5274.77 ± 1353.26 mm 3 vs. 3215.20 ± 1524.84 mm 3 ), higher cam/head ratios (8.61% ± 2.02% vs. 6.35% ± 1.97%), and more superolateral lesions (52.4% vs. 36.2% anterior in the fracture group) (all p < 0.001). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses identified cohort‐specific discriminatory values of 66° for alpha angle (AUC, 0.884), 4421 mm 3 for cam volume (AUC, 0.839), and 6.4% for the cam‐to‐head volume ratio (AUC, 0.791). In multivariable analyses using continuous morphology measures, higher alpha angle, greater cam volume, higher cam‐to‐head volume ratio, and superolateral lesion location were associated with end‐stage OA‐group membership. Conclusions Compared with non‐arthritic cam‐positive hips in an elderly fracture cohort, end‐stage primary OA hips had greater three‐dimensional cam burden, with lesions more often located superolaterally. These retrospective associations do not establish longitudinal progression, causality, or individual prognosis. Study Design Retrospective comparative study. Level of Evidence Level III, study of a non‐consecutive patients, study of diagnostic test.

papers.title: Long-Term Risk of Lumbar Fusion Surgery Following Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: A Nationwide Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Objective: To assess the long-term incidence of lumbar fusion surgery and its risk factors following total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA), using data from a South Korean nationwide cohort.Methods: The analysis included 528 patients who underwent THA and 2,978 who underwent TKA during 2005-2013, together with controls propensity-matched at a 1:20 ratio by age, sex, and screening year.The primary outcome was subsequent lumbar fusion surgery, identified from National Health Insurance Service procedure codes.Cox models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs), and subgroup analyses were conducted by age, sex, body mass index, cholesterol level, and income.Results: Over a mean follow-up of 3.5 years for THA and 2.8 years for TKA, the risk of lumbar fusion surgery was significantly higher after THA (aHR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-6.22)and TKA (aHR, 1.97; 95% CI, 1.46-2.67)than among matched controls.The associations were stronger in men than in women and in adults aged ≥60 years than in younger adults.Among patients who underwent TKA, overweight status, lower cholesterol levels, and higher income were associated with higher risk.Conclusion: Compared with matched controls, patients who underwent THA or TKA had a higher long-term risk of subsequent lumbar fusion surgery.This association was stronger in older adults and men.These findings emphasize the importance of considering lumbar spine health in the care of patients undergoing lower limb arthroplasty.

papers.title: CrossBlend physics-informed LSTM for nonlinear structural response prediction within a cyber-physical framework
papers.abstract: This study develops and evaluates physics-informed deep learning models for predicting nonlinear seismic structural responses within a cyber-physical framework. Four variants of Physics-Informed Long Short-Term Memory (PhyLSTM) models are proposed: baseline windowed and full-sequence PhyLSTM models and their CrossBlend counterparts. The CrossBlend mechanism implements a learnable dual-path displacement blending mechanism within the PhyLSTM framework, in which a sequence-level and floor-wise gating parameter adaptively combines direct displacement prediction with a velocity-integrated displacement pathway, while embedding dynamic equilibrium equation residuals as physics-based constraints to enhance long-sequence stability and mitigate cumulative displacement prediction drift. The models are trained and validated using finite element (FE) simulation data from three structural configurations with varying levels of nonlinearity, and evaluated against experimental datasets through two single-stage strategies, namely baseline cyber-domain training and weighted training, and three two-stage strategies, namely fine-tuning, partial-freeze tuning, and teacher-student training. The CrossBlend-PhyLSTM models outperform the baseline PhyLSTM models in displacement prediction accuracy, achieving mean correlation coefficients of 0.96–0.98 compared to 0.85–0.88 for the baseline models under the most nonlinear structural configuration. A controlled ablation analysis further confirms that the proposed CrossBlend models provides the strongest overall displacement prediction performance compared with the direct-only, integrated-only, and fixed-blending alternatives. Two-stage fine-tuning emerges as the most effective cross-domain adaptation approach, substantially improving prediction accuracy across all structural configurations compared with baseline cyber-domain training. These results establish the CrossBlend-PhyLSTM models as reliable structure-specific surrogate predictors for real-time structural response evaluation and digital twin applications.

papers.title: Autoencoder-based non-intrusive model order reduction for anisotropic and multi-physics problems
papers.abstract: Abstract We propose a non-intrusive, Autoencoder-based framework for reduced-order modeling in continuum mechanics. Our method integrates three stages: (i) an unsupervised Autoencoder compresses high-dimensional finite element solutions into a compact latent space, (ii) a supervised regression network maps problem parameters to latent codes, and (iii) an end-to-end surrogate reconstructs full-field solutions directly from input parameters. To overcome limitations of existing approaches, we propose two key extensions: a force-augmented variant that jointly predicts displacement fields and reaction forces at Neumann boundaries, and a multi-field architecture that enables coupled field predictions, such as in thermo-mechanical systems. The framework is validated on nonlinear benchmark problems involving heterogeneous composites, anisotropic elasticity with geometric variation, and thermo-mechanical coupling. Across all cases, it achieves accurate reconstructions of high-fidelity solutions while remaining fully non-intrusive. These results highlight the potential of combining deep learning with dimensionality reduction to build efficient and extensible surrogate models.

papers.title: Bioengineering technologies for enabling biomedical research in space
papers.abstract: Sustained human presence in space requires research platforms capable of capturing the physiological consequences of microgravity, radiation, and isolation, while operating within the severe mass, volume, and crew-time constraints of orbital missions. This review surveys bioengineering strategies that have been adapted to meet these demands: tissue engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, tissue chips, and biosensors. Tissue-engineered constructs and human stem cell‐derived organoids provide human-relevant alternatives to animal models and exploit the absence of gravitational settling to generate more uniform, complex multicellular structures, though vascularization and long-term functional stability remain unresolved challenges. 3D bioprinting in microgravity reduces construct collapse and sedimentation-driven defects, and extrusion-based platforms such as the ISS BioFabrication Facility have already demonstrated in-flight tissue printing, though mechanical equivalence to native tissue and photopolymerization-based approaches remain areas of active development. Tissue chips offer a small-footprint, human-specific alternative to traditional cell culture and have been used to model organ systems ranging from cardiac and skeletal muscle tissue to the blood‐brain barrier, supporting both disease modeling and radiation countermeasure testing in orbit. Biosensors, whether deployed independently or integrated with tissue chip platforms, enable real-time, in‐situ data collection that reduces reliance on crew time and sample return. Together, these technologies are converging toward unified, autonomous platforms for tissue fabrication, culture, and monitoring in space. We discuss the current state, limitations, and future directions of each approach, and highlight the opportunities for their integration to advance both astronaut health and terrestrial regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Hypersonic flutter analysis and uncertainty quantification of composite honeycomb wing plates with various Poisson's ratios
papers.abstract: Composite honeycomb structures mitigate aeroelastic instabilities in high-speed vehicles, yet predicting their flutter boundaries under thermo-structural uncertainties remains challenging. This paper presents a comprehensive computational framework to investigate the hypersonic aerothermoelastic flutter of cantilever trapezoidal plates with an orthotropic honeycomb core. By coupling first-order shear deformation theory (FSDT) with hypersonic piston theory and incorporating thermal stress effects, the governing equations are efficiently solved using a coordinate-transformed differential quadrature method (DQM). A distinct feature of this study is the integration of Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) to perform rigorous uncertainty quantification, transitioning the analysis from a deterministic approach to a robust system assessment. Furthermore, a comparative analysis evaluating discrete Poisson's ratio configurations (negative, zero, and positive) is systematically conducted. Validated against finite element and experimental data, our parametric investigations reveal that the negative Poisson's ratio (auxetic) core exhibits enhanced aeroelastic robustness and higher critical flutter boundaries compared to its zero and positive counterparts. Crucially, our parametric and sensitivity analyses reveal that specific core thickness configurations can significantly enhance natural frequencies and elevate critical flutter speeds under elevated temperatures. These results help engineers expand flutter boundaries and balance weight-to-stiffness in high-speed vehicles.

papers.title: Structural lightweight design of bogie bolster based on surrogate models
papers.abstract: The bogie bolster is one of the key components of railway freight cars, and its lightweight design plays an important role in improving the transportation capacity of freight vehicles. However, the bolster features complex geometry, leading to high costs and long design cycles in structural development. In this paper, finite element analysis (FEA) is performed to evaluate the static strength and stiffness of the bolster. An optimization model is established taking the geometric dimensions of process holes as design variables, the minimum mass of the bolster as objective function, and allowable stress and deformation as constraint conditions. The Kriging surrogate model is constructed for mass, stress and deformation responses. Then expected improvement (EI) criterion is adopted for sample infilling to improve model prediction performance, and genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to solve the optimization problem. Global Sobol sensitivity analysis is further implemented to quantify the contribution of each design variable to structural responses. After obtaining the lightweight scheme, finite-element-based fatigue simulation and modal characteristic analysis are carried out for post-verification to assess the service reliability of the optimized bolster. Numerical results show that the optimized structure satisfies the static-strength and stiffness constraints in the optimization formulation. Post-verification demonstrates that the optimized structure also meets fatigue and modal-performance specifications. The total mass of the bogie bolster is reduced by 16.20 kg, achieving the lightweight target for heavy-duty freight bogie bolsters.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of metallic implants: a comprehensive review of material selection, porous architecture, and hybrid surface engineering
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) of metallic implants is shifting from geometry replication toward integrated control of load transfer, tissue interaction, and surface stability. Nevertheless, the literature remains fragmented, often optimizing biomaterials, architectures, AM processes, and bioactive coatings as separate components despite their coupled performance. This review proposes an integrated design framework that connects patient anatomy, material selection, architected porosity, AM technology, and hybrid surface engineering into a unified development pathway. CT/MRI-based design and topology optimization are presented for a lattice topology, with the aim of achieving precise volumetric porosity levels between 50% and 85% to bring effective stiffness into the physiological range of human bone, approximately 0.01–20 GPa. Titanium, Co-Cr alloys, and 316L stainless steel, as well as magnesium alloys, are critically compared with hydroxyapatite, bioactive glass, and hierarchical hybrid coatings to demonstrate how multilayer functionality can overcome limitations of metallic substrates. Coating performance correlates with adhesion, degradation, and cellular response, which treats biological evaluation as an interconnected metric rather than an isolated endpoint. It discusses critical trade-offs where increased porosity improves mechanical compatibility, but retention of fatigue strength above cortical bone thresholds of 40–60 MPa remains a profound manufacturing challenge; increased coating complexity increases the risk of interfacial failure, and accelerated degradation compromises retention of structural integrity. The review concludes by identifying manufacturing reproducibility, coating durability on complex lattices, and regulatory qualification as the leading barriers to clinical translation.

papers.title: Preoperative pain and achievement of the minimal clinically important difference for physical function one year after total hip arthroplasty: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine the association between preoperative social, clinical, and biological variables and the achievement of the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) on the WOMAC-function subscale one year post total hip arthroplasty (THA). METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 85 patients (aged ≥ 65) completed baseline preoperative assessment, and 53 completed the 12-month follow-up (32 lost to follow-up; 66.0% achieved MCID). The outcome was achieving WOMAC-function MCID (≥ 26.54 points). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for baseline pain, age, sex, and BMI were performed. ROC curves evaluated discriminative capacity. RESULTS: An exploratory ROC analysis identified a baseline pain threshold of 6.5 on the Numerical Rating Scale yielded an AUC of 0.740 (70% sensitivity, 77% specificity). CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative pain intensity independently associated with clinically meaningful functional improvement post-THA. An exploratory pain threshold of 6.5 on the NRS may provide an exploratory benchmark for future risk stratification.

papers.title: A multiscale physics-informed neural network with RVE homogenization using isogeometric analysis for hygrothermal-electro-mechanical coupled analysis of piezoelectric composites
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have shown potential for coupled field analysis, but their application to heterogeneous piezoelectric composites under combined thermal and moisture effects remains limited because the effective properties depend on the microstructure and the residuals of the coupled governing equations may differ substantially in scale. This paper develops a multiscale method for hygrothermal-electro-mechanical coupled analysis of piezoelectric composites. At the microscale, a representative volume element of a 1–3 piezoelectric composite is constructed, in which the cylindrical fibers are exactly represented by NURBS basis functions. The effective properties of the composite are then computed by isogeometric analysis. At the macroscale, the homogenized properties are incorporated into a parametric physics-informed neural network to predict structural responses under multiple loading and environmental conditions. The network takes the coordinates, load amplitude, temperature increment and moisture concentration increment as inputs. A nondimensional formulation is introduced to reduce training instability caused by the scale disparity among the governing equation residuals. Numerical examples show that the proposed method obtains accurate effective properties with relatively few control points. The predicted hygrothermal-electro-mechanical coupled responses agree well with the reference solutions. The proposed method provides an effective tool for multiscale modeling and response analysis of piezoelectric composites in hygrothermal environments.

papers.title: Accelerometry-based comparison of functional outcomes across total and partial knee and hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Aims: To evaluate objectively measured physical activity after hip and knee arthroplasty using accelerometry, by comparing bone-preserving procedures with total athorpalsties rthorpalsties and benchmarking both against non-arthritic controls. Methods: This observational study was conducted within the UK Biobank. Adults aged 40 to 69 years with total knee arthroplasty (TKA), unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA), total hip arthroplasty (THA), or hip resurfacing (HR) were identified through linked hospital records and completed seven-day wrist-worn accelerometry (Axivity AX3). Outcomes included adjusted daily step count (primary), peak cadence, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and Euclidean Norm Minus One (ENMO). Surgical groups were propensity score-matched to non-arthritic controls on demographics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Direct comparisons between procedure types were examined using both propensity-matched analyses and complementary multivariable regression, and adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates. Subgroup analyses considered < 12 months and ≥12 months post-surgery. Results: A total of 2,283 participants were included (TKA = 860, UKA = 162, THA = 1,168, HR = 93). Compared with matched controls, TKA and THA patients showed persistently lower activity, while UKA and HR achieved levels similar to controls. In the knee cohort, UKA patients walked significantly more steps/day than TKA (9,150 vs 7,920; + 15.5%, p < 0.001) with higher cadence. In the hip cohort, HR patients outperformed THA (10,122 vs 9,139 steps/day; + 10.6%, p = 0.032) and demonstrated higher peak cadence, and HR remained comparable to controls. All groups fell within the 'somewhat active' to 'active' step-count range (7,500 to 12,499 steps/day). Conclusion: UKA and HR are associated with higher postoperative activity compared with total arthroplasty (TKA, THA). Accelerometry provides an objective, scalable assessment of functional recovery, highlighting procedure-specific differences that should be considered alongside implant longevity when selecting surgical options.

papers.title: Stellar blend image classification using computationally efficient Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Stellar blends, where two or more stars appear blended in an image, pose a significant visualization challenge in astronomy. Traditionally, distinguishing these blends from single stars has been costly and resource-intensive, involving sophisticated equipment and extensive expert analysis. This is especially problematic for analyzing the vast data volumes from surveys, such as Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), Legacy Imaging Survey and the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF). To address these challenges, we apply different normalizations and data embeddings on low resolution images of single stars and stellar blends, which are passed as inputs into machine learning methods and to a computationally efficient Gaussian process model (MuyGPs). MuyGPs consistently outperforms the benchmarked models, particularly on limited training data. Moreover, under the corresponding preprocessing and embedding pipeline, MuyGPs with rth root local min-max normalization achieved 83.8% accuracy. Furthermore, because MuyGPs provides predictive uncertainty estimates, it may be useful in downstream human-in-the-loop workflows, such as flagging low-confidence predictions for specialist review.

papers.title: Evaluating Statistical Downscaling Techniques for Regional Hydroclimatic Change Projections Over CONUS
papers.abstract: Abstract Projecting the impacts of future climate change is critical for water managers planning infrastructure resilience strategies. Global earth system model output is generally too coarse to provide the detailed, localized information needed for impact assessment, and the computational cost of running higher‐resolution global simulations over sufficiently long periods is prohibitive. Downscaling methods span a wide range of computational cost, and statistical approaches in particular offer a relatively inexpensive way to refine climate model output into a more actionable form. Here, we assess a broad suite of statistical and simplified dynamic downscaling approaches for nine regions across the coterminous United States (CONUS). We develop a suite of metrics to evaluate these methods, including a novel assessment of method performance under dominant large‐scale meteorological conditions identified using a k‐means weather‐typing algorithm along with traditionally used measures of precipitation and temperature, such as seasonal means and spatial variability, and representations of teleconnection patterns associated with El Niño–Southern Oscillation. We also include multiple observational data sets to account for observational uncertainty. This framework enables uncertainty quantification associated with climate model forcing, downscaling method choice, and observational data set selection on a per metric basis. Downscaled data set subselection using our evaluation can substantially alter the magnitude of the projected change signal, but rarely alters the sign of change when compared with the ensemble average. Further, by quantifying regional downscaling method performance, we can provide actionable guidance to decision makers on the most appropriate downscaling data set or method for a given application.

papers.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
papers.abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from $ab$ $initio$ calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the $ab$ $initio$ procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $α$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $α$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $Γ$ and $Γ'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,Γ,Γ',J,g_c)=(-6.0,\,7.5,\,-0.3,\,-1.75,\,2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $Γ'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $Γ$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$Γ$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with experiment. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.

papers.title: Adjoint method versus physics-informed neural networks in PDE-constrained inverse problems
papers.abstract: Inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) are central to computational mechanics and are commonly solved by adjoint-based optimization, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a flexible alternative. Their relative performance remains difficult to assess because the two approaches are often compared under different formulations, parameterizations, optimizers, and regularization choices. We present a controlled comparison of adjoint optimization and PINNs for PDE-constrained inverse problems. From a common abstract formulation, we instantiate both methods on identical domains, governing equations, observation models, and regularization terms, while matching the optimizer, unknown parameterization, and arithmetic precision wherever applicable. The benchmarks include unsteady Burgers, noisy Darcy permeability inversion, three-dimensional Allen–Cahn reaction identification, and unsteady Navier–Stokes viscosity identification. The results show that the representation of the unknown largely determines the preferred method: grid-based fields favor the discrete adjoint, whereas neural representations are native to PINNs and relevant for closure and constitutive modeling. For time-dependent problems, adjoint inversion can be dominated by trajectory storage and differentiation, while PINNs provide satisfactory reconstructions at lower cost. A PINN-warm-started adjoint strategy then recovers adjoint-level accuracy at about half the cost.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
papers.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

papers.title: Neural surrogate-based model predictive control for compressed air energy storage
papers.abstract: Compressed air energy storage is a promising technology for large-scale, long-duration energy storage in renewable-integrated power systems. However, accurate modeling and control of compressed air energy storage under realistic operating conditions remain challenging due to the tightly coupled thermodynamic processes involving multi-stage compression, heat exchange, cavern storage, and expansion, all of which interact under off-design conditions. This thesis develops a learning-based framework for the modeling and control of adiabatic compressed air energy storage systems under off-design operating conditions. A detailed thermodynamic model of the compressed air energy storage system is first developed to capture component-level off-design behavior, including variable isentropic efficiencies, expansion ratios, and load-dependent heat exchanger dynamics. Neural controlled differential equation models are then trained on two complementary datasets: component-level off-design performance maps and system-level sequential operational trajectories. The learned surrogates are integrated within a model predictive control framework applied to a wind-diesel-compressed air energy storage hybrid energy system representative of a remote northern community. Different neural controlled differential equation modeling formulations are introduced, including extensions of input structures to incorporate control-relevant decision variables, and evaluated across multiple dimensions: generalization to unseen operating conditions, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and computational efficiency benchmarking against the full thermodynamic model. A robustness analysis under additive Gaussian forecast noise confirms that the model predictive control framework maintains its fundamental dispatch character under degraded forecast quality. The developed methodology contributes to advancing the modeling, optimization, and control of compressed air energy storage systems under real-world operating conditions, supporting the broader integration of large-scale energy storage in renewable-powered grids.

papers.title: Substantial disagreement between satellite- and ground-level nighttime light patterns revealed by SDGSAT-1 and street view imagery
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, nighttime light (NTL) has become one of the most widely used and powerful proxies for characterizing human activities. Despite the recent proliferation of available NTL data from both satellite- and ground-level sensors, intrinsic differences between these two observation approaches can result in distinct NTL brightness patterns (satellite-ground disagreement). Such disagreement, particularly its spatial heterogeneity, represents a critical yet largely overlooked issue in NTL studies, introducing uncertainty into the interpretation and application of NTL observations. Here, by incorporating SDGSAT-1 glimmer imagery and panoramic nighttime street view imagery with geospatial AI approaches, we present a spatially explicit, wall-to-wall investigation into satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Specifically, we characterized citywide disagreement and its variation across land-use types, analyzed contributing factors, and assessed its implications for NTL-based applications, reinforced by Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analyses using independent observations from Singapore and Shenzhen, China. Our study revealed substantial and spatially heterogeneous satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Relative disagreement averaged 15% ± 13% citywide but reached 42% ± 12% in 13% of the city. Such pronounced heterogeneity was likewise evident across land-use types, with commercial areas standing out for consistently significant disagreement, where ground-level NTL brightness was 29% ± 26% higher than satellite-level NTL brightness. Building morphology, vegetation canopy cover, and sensor spectral response contributed to satellite-ground disagreement, suggestive of distinct mechanisms underlying the identified patterns. Applying satellite- and ground-level NTL data yielded relative differences of at least 115% and 83% in GDP estimation and NTL exposure inequality assessment, respectively. This study sheds new light on satellite-ground disagreement by moving beyond discrete comparisons toward a comprehensive analysis of its heterogeneity and implications, thereby establishing an empirical basis for integrating NTL observations and contributing to more reliable NTL-based applications and evidence-informed policies on sustainable urbanization.

papers.title: Machine learning assisted rapid screening of multi-element doped solid-state electrolyte materials
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles and energy storage systems, solid-state batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their high safety, energy density, and long cycle life. The solid-state electrolyte is the core component, but developing high-performance and stable materials remains a major challenge. This study focuses on Li 3 PS 4 and applies a multi-element co-doping strategy (Si, Ge, Sn at the P site). Combined with machine learning, we efficiently identify thermodynamically stable candidates and narrow the search scope. Our framework incorporates physically informed feature engineering, systematic hyperparameter tuning and stacking ensemble (XGBoost, LightGBM, RandomForest), SHAP analysis, uncertainty quantification (90% prediction intervals with actual coverages of 93.2% and 90.2%), and active learning simulation. Beyond the specific predictions, this work establishes a generalizable screening paradigm that integrates interpretable ML prediction, softBV-based kinetic ranking, and DFT-validated property assessment, enabling holistic evaluation of multi-component doped electrolytes. Using these methods, we rapidly screen several promising candidates with superior ion transport properties. The model achieves test R 2 = 0.879 for formation energy and 0.967 for energy above hull.

papers.title: Modelling heterogeneous interface diffusion kinetics via a retinal-inspired hierarchical focal-PINN
papers.abstract: To resolve the fundamental conflict between suppressing measurement noise and capturing localised kinetic features in heterogeneous interface diffusion prediction, a novel Topology-Aware Hierarchical Focal-PINN is proposed, incorporating a retinal-inspired hierarchical focusing mechanism. Mimicking the biological fovea, the model addresses the spectral bias of traditional PINNs through residual-triggered hierarchical refinement with adjacency-aware subdomain control. This architecture enables multi-scale signal separation: global regularisation suppresses unstructured instrumental noise, while micro-scale focused weighting amplifies sensitivity to localised kinetic anomalies. Experimental results on the copper-stainless steel system demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms Global-PINN, reducing the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 0.844 μm to 0.203 μm (∼76% reduction) and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by ∼68%. With a coefficient of determination (R²) reaching 0.991, the model effectively resolves the bottleneck of high-fidelity modelling for complex interfacial diffusion phenomena.

papers.title: Nonlinear pipe–soil–liner interaction of corroded steel pipelines rehabilitated with FRP liners under differential ground settlement
papers.abstract: Differential ground settlement can produce severe localized deformation in corroded water-supply pipelines. This study develops an idealized three-dimensional nonlinear finite element model of a corroded X65 steel pipe rehabilitated with a close-fitting, unbonded fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) liner under monotonic quasi-static settlement. The pipe–soil component of the framework is partially verified against an existing full-scale reverse-fault test. The generic liner is represented by a simplified isotropic elastic–perfectly plastic law, and 160 MPa is used as an interpretive tensile-stress threshold. Under the baseline calculation at a settlement displacement of 0.30 m, the computed steel-pipe peak strain is 22.5% lower with the liner; however, the liner reaches its stated stress threshold at approximately 0.24 m. Results beyond the first component threshold are therefore reported only as constitutive trends and are not used to claim safe capacity. Local corrosion increases the peak steel strain by approximately 155%, and the most unfavorable investigated defect location is 1.1 m from the settlement interface. Increasing soil stiffness intensifies strain localization, whereas increasing liner stiffness reduces steel strain while increasing liner stress and reducing the settlement required to reach the liner threshold. The present study quantifies conditional quasi-static resistance indicators, not time-dependent system resilience. Orthotropic progressive damage, calibrated bond–slip, gradual settlement profiles, and uncertainty quantification remain necessary for design-level conclusions.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Healthcare regulation in the Amazonian state of Pará faces geographic barriers, unequal connectivity, and fragmented access to specialized care. Objective: to report the experience of planning and conducting e-SUS Regulação implementation workshops across Pará's 13 Health Regions. Method: descriptive experience report with a qualitative approach, based on three-day theoretical and practical workshops held in 2025 and 2026, grounded in Continuing Health Education and active learning methods. The activities involved 299 managers and regulation professionals linked to the state's 144 municipalities. Results: training addressed four operational profiles (Administrator, Requester, Regulator, and Provider), combining simulations based on the actual healthcare network, data from the National Registry of Health Facilities, word clouds, and an interactive quiz. The Rio Caetés and Metropolitana III Health Regions began using the system routinely, particularly to regulate Integrated Care Offerings in Cardiology, Orthopedics, Surgical Risk Assessment, and Women's Health under the Agora Tem Especialistas Program. Unstable connectivity and turnover of municipal health workers remain major challenges. Final considerations: the experience highlights the importance of continuous, regionally adapted training linked to intergovernmental governance to sustain system implementation. Systematic assessment of healthcare outcomes is still needed.

papers.title: Validating car-following behaviors of autonomous vehicles by structural assessment with empirical data
papers.abstract: Abstract Many researchers argue that the modular perception–planning–control design of autonomous vehicles (AVs) inevitably introduces delays, yet how such delays influence car-following behaviors and what their magnitudes are remain uncertain due to limited empirical data and ineffective calibration methods. Using large-scale naturalistic autonomous vehicle trajectory data, we develop an optimization-based calibration framework that jointly estimates feedback delay in perception/decision and parasitic lag in actuation, and accommodates both linear constant-time-headway and nonlinear intelligent-driver-model controllers. The method combines Bayesian optimization (BO) for globally searching delay parameters with simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) for efficiently tuning controller parameters. Results show that incorporating both delays substantially improves model accuracy, reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) by up to an order of magnitude compared with models without delays, while linear controllers reproduce AV trajectories more faithfully and local calibration proves more accurate for short horizons whereas global calibration is more reliable for long horizons.

papers.title: Diagnosing and correcting openet satellite evapotranspiration across us climate zones: Error decomposition, explainable AI, and uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Satellite evapotranspiration (ET) from the OpenET platform supports water resource management across the United States but exhibits biases that vary by climate. While machine learning (ML) can improve satellite ET accuracy, prior studies report aggregate metrics without explaining how corrections work or providing operational uncertainty quantification. This study applies an XGBoost correction framework integrating OpenET satellite outputs with ground meteorological observations from 22 AmeriFlux cropland eddy covariance sites across six Köppen climate zones. The framework achieved 41.9% RMSE improvement over OpenET, while a configuration excluding all ground meteorological inputs still achieved 28.5% improvement. Error decomposition revealed that the dominant correction mechanism shifts seasonally: summer corrections were driven primarily by bias removal (61.3% of improvement), reflecting systematic overestimation during peak ET, while winter corrections were driven by variance reduction (96.8%), addressing satellite noise from cloud contamination. Across climates, humid zones improved primarily through variance reduction (68–81%), while water limited zones, including BSk and dry-summer Csa sites, benefited more from bias correction (40–52%). SHAP analysis stratified by climate yielded patterns consistent with these mechanisms. Leave-one-site-out cross-validation indicated strong transferability in humid climates (Dwb R² = 0.82) but limited generalization in BSk sites (R² = −0.30), while leave-one-cluster-out validation provided a more conservative spatial-transferability estimate by accounting for colocated site clusters. Conformal prediction provided empirical uncertainty quantification: constant-width intervals achieved 92.6% overall coverage, while climate-adaptive intervals produced environment specific uncertainty bounds ranging from ±0.81 to ±2.13 mm/day across climates. This framework provides a pathway toward operational ET correction with uncertainty bounds and diagnostic insights for satellite algorithm improvement.

papers.title: A PROPOSED KALIMUTHU GEOMETRIC FRAMEWORK FOR COLLISION-RISK REDUCTION IN MULTI-UAV SYSTEMS
papers.abstract: Autonomous drones must continuously maintain safe separation from other aircraft, obstacles, and dynamically changing flight corridors. Existing collision-avoidance research uses geometric guidance, velocity-obstacle methods, optimization, model predictive control, potential fields, probabilistic reasoning, and learning-based approaches. This article proposes a new research direction: a Kalimuthu Geometric Collision-Avoidance Framework (KGCAF) in which Kalimuthu calculus, manifolds, configurations, frameworks, and geometry are treated as a mathematical layer for representing, monitoring, and regulating near-collision states in three dimensional flight space. The central hypothesis is that a drone encounter can be represented as a continuously evolving geometric configuration whose boundary, degeneration, separation margin, and admissible transition can be computed before physical intersection occurs. Degenerate configurations are interpreted not merely as failures of geometry, but as boundary states that can trigger conservative avoidance actions. The proposed framework combines relative position, relative velocity, safety envelopes, configuration manifolds, boundary transition rules, and a Lyapunov-compatible control layer. It introduces measurable quantities— configuration distance, normalized separation, boundary proximity, predicted time-to-conflict, and geometric risk index—that can be compared against conventional methods. The article does not claim that Kalimuthu methods have already prevented drone collisions; instead, it formulates testable hypotheses and a reproducible validation program involving simulation, hardware-in the-loop experiments, and controlled flight trials. If validated, the framework could provide a mathematically transparent alternative or complement to existing multi-UAV collision-avoidance architectures.

papers.title: Primary versus conversion hemiarthroplasty after failed internal fixation for intertrochanteric fractures: a multicenter retrospective study
papers.abstract: Conversion hemiarthroplasty (CHA) following failed internal fixation of intertrochanteric fractures is a technically demanding procedure, yet direct comparisons with primary hemiarthroplasty (PHA) are scarce. This study compared the perioperative characteristics, postoperative complications, survival outcomes, and mid-term clinical outcomes between patients undergoing PHA and those requiring CHA. This multicenter retrospective study included 147 patients who underwent hemiarthroplasty for intertrochanteric fractures at three tertiary hospitals between March 2009 and September 2025, including 42 who underwent PHA and 105 who underwent CHA after failed internal fixation. Perioperative characteristics, postoperative complications, 1-year mortality, and postoperative pain and hip function were compared between groups. Implant-related variables, including femoral stem type, fixation method, and greater trochanter reconstruction, were also evaluated. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression were performed to assess survival outcomes and factors associated with complication-free survival. Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable between the groups. Compared with PHA, CHA was associated with significantly longer operative time, greater intraoperative blood loss, longer hospital stay, higher postoperative VAS scores, and lower postoperative HHS values at the 24-month follow-up (all P < 0.0001). The overall postoperative complication rate was also significantly higher in the CHA group. By contrast, intraoperative transfusion, limb-length discrepancy, and 1-year mortality were numerically more frequent in the CHA group, but these differences were not statistically significant. CHA more often required long stems, cemented femoral components, and plate-and-screw fixation of the greater trochanter. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly worse overall survival and complication-free survival in the CHA group, whereas multivariable Cox regression identified a higher age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index as an independent predictor of poorer complication-free survival. Conversion hemiarthroplasty following failed internal fixation of intertrochanteric fractures involved greater operative complexity and resulted in worse postoperative pain and function than primary hemiarthroplasty. The postoperative course was also less favorable. In addition, overall survival and complication-free survival differed significantly between the groups.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Tools into English Language Teaching: Opportunities and Challenges for Teachers
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has shifted from supportive digital tools to more sophisticated systems with an active learning and teaching function. The present study discusses literature between 2021 and mid-2025 on the use of AI tools in English Language Teaching (ELT), with a specific concentration on teachers' attitudes, potential, and concerns. A PRISMA-guided methodology drove the search and screening of 65 peer-reviewed papers, case studies, and practitioners' reports from around the globe. The review classifies main categories of AI applications, including adaptive learning systems, automatic evaluation systems, conversational agents, translation and multimodal tools, and AI literacy tools. The evidence points to potential benefits, such as personalized learning, productivity gains for teachers, enhanced learner engagement, and enhanced access for students from low-resourced environments. Simultaneously, key issues are flagged concerning pedagogy, infrastructure, teacher education, ethics, privacy, and professional identity. Case studies report on actual teacher and student experiences using ChatGPT, Duolingo, and Grammarly, illustrating possibilities as well as dangers for classroom adoption. The review further points towards the incorporation of AI literacy in teacher training, provision of ongoing professional development, and building critical digital literacy. The findings first and foremost signal that the successful use of AI in ELT should appropriately weigh teaching methods and technological innovation, moral rights, and contextualization in their upholding of fairness and longevity.

papers.abstract: This article examines the integration of international organization simulations with Education 4.0 tools as a strategy to innovate teaching in International Relations. Higher education faces declining engagement and a growing demand for active learning methods. Simulations of international organizations, such as the Organization of American States (OAS), have proven effective in fostering student participation and critical thinking skills. This study reports on a hybrid pedagogical project conducted in Brazil in 2024, which combined preparatory workshops, a mock simulation, the main OAS General Assembly simulation, and a structured debriefing. Data collection included pre- and post-simulation self-assessment questionnaires, reflective reports, and text analysis (term frequency-inverse TF-IDF and cosine similarity) of the Official Position Papers (OPPs) and final documents. The findings indicate significant gains in conceptual mastery, methodological preference, and motivation to continue studies, with average self-assessment scores rising by 31.8%. Reflective reports highlighted skills such as negotiation, leadership, and collaborative writing. Text analysis revealed how students mobilized terms related to crisis management, cooperation, and institutional strengthening, while cosine similarity demonstrated that final documents were shaped more by negotiation dynamics than by initial OPPs. These results confirm the dual value of simulations as pedagogical tools and laboratories for consensus-building, aligning experiential learning with the competencies demanded by Education 4.0.

papers.title: Biomachining in manufacturing: mechanisms, processes, applications and future perspectives
papers.abstract: Biomachining (BM) is an emerging bio-assisted manufacturing approach that uses microbial metabolism and bioelectrochemical reactions to remove material under mild conditions. Due to its low mechanical loading and limited thermal effects, BM has potential in low-damage microfabrication, surface functionalization, microfluidic mold fabrication, abrasive tool dressing, and functional device modification. This review critically summarizes BM with respect to removal mechanisms, process technologies, modeling and optimization strategies, manufacturing applications, and engineering challenges. The biological and electrochemical mechanisms of BM are discussed first, followed by conventional and hybrid BM processes and their comparison with conventional and non-conventional machining technologies. Current applications are reviewed with emphasis on the gap between laboratory demonstrations and scalable industrial implementation. Major challenges include low removal efficiency, limited dimensional accuracy, unstable microbial activity, weak process controllability, contamination risk, waste treatment, and biosafety management. Future development should focus on standardized evaluation, microbial stability control, mechanism-data fusion modeling, hybrid process intensification, and dedicated equipment. Machine learning-assisted prediction, Internet of Things-enabled monitoring, digital twin-based closed-loop control, and sustainability/techno-economic validation are also important for moving BM toward controllable and scalable manufacturing.

papers.title: Milti-layer homocentric sphere and spherical symmetry for rogue wave light bullets in three-dimensional high-order nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We discover multi-layer homocentric spherical structures of rogue-wave light bullets in the spherically reduced (3+1)-dimensional higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equation (HNLSE). These solutions belong to the ℓ = 0 invariant subspace of the full 3D operator and satisfy the complete radial equation exactly. These optical spheres are spherically reduced rogue-wave light bullets: they are localized in all three spatial directions and transient in time, but, unlike conventional traveling light bullets, they are stationary in the sense that their isosurfaces oscillate radially without translating -a localization arising from the rogue-wave nature extended to three dimensions, revealing single-, two-, and four-layer concentric spherical shells. We present also a linear-stability analysis of the optical sphere solutions. For the spherically reduced background, we derive the radial eigenvalue problem and identify the parameter regimes in which the background is modulationally unstable. A full nonlinear stability analysis remains an open problem. We uses the PINN framework to numerically simulate the rogue wave solutions in the HNLSE, and verifies the solution by comparing it with the exact analytical solution to confirm the solution accuracy. The multi-layer homocentric sphere with preserved spherical symmetry serves as the definitive fingerprint of the 3D rogue-wave light bullet, with implications for nonlinear optics, Bose–Einstein condensates, and ocean wave dynamics.

papers.title: Anchor placement optimization in outdoor UWB systems for pedestrian-surrogate localization
papers.abstract: This study proposes a novel framework for optimizing outdoor ultra-wideband (UWB) anchor placement to support real-time pedestrian-surrogate localization. This framework comprises three key characteristics. First, a localization error is quantified to evaluate the positioning performance of candidate anchor configurations. This quantification enables direct estimation of three-dimensional positioning errors under realistic outdoor propagation conditions. Second, radio-frequency coverage is quantified by employing min–max normalization to the received-signal-strength measurements. Antenna orientation and anchor height effects are incorporated to evaluate communication stability under diverse deployment conditions. Third, Bayesian optimization is performed using a hybrid objective function that simultaneously accounts for coverage robustness and localization accuracy. The contributions of these characteristics to pedestrian-surrogate localization are verified through controlled experiments examining ranging distortions and signal degradation. Extensive field experiments in diverse outdoor environments also confirm communication stability and improved localization accuracy under the optimized anchor configurations obtained from the proposed framework. This framework provides novel guidelines for outdoor UWB anchor placement, enabling adaptation across diverse deployment environments and operational conditions.

papers.title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning using a world model for multi-objective optimization of micro-milling
papers.abstract: Existing micro-milling optimization methods often rely on fixed objective weights or direct parameter control, limiting their ability to handle state-dependent trade-offs among surface quality, energy consumption, and machining time. This study proposes a preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic framework with a learned world model for sequential parameter optimization. Unlike direct-parameter reinforcement learning, the proposed method separates objective-level preference learning from feasible command generation. A high-level Dirichlet policy selects an interpretable preference vector over surface quality, energy, and time, while a constrained inverse control module maps it to spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut within prescribed bounds and rate limits. A multimodal temporal convolutional gated recurrent unit (MTC-GRU) world model trained on 900 physical Ti-6Al-4V micro-milling trials serves as the rollout environment for policy learning. Controller performance is evaluated through closed-loop rollouts within the frozen learned environment, while three predetermined variable-parameter trajectories, each physically replayed nine times, are used to assess recursive world-model fidelity under low, medium, and high transition intensities. Within the learned environment, preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic (PC-HAC) improves surface quality, energy use, and machining time under the stationary objective, and achieves larger gains in the cumulative energy-budget task. At κ = 0.80, PC-HAC reduced the budget-penalized score by 53.9% relative to the greedy controller. The recursive physical replay evaluation yields overall R 2 values of 0.810 for surface roughness and 0.975 for energy, with prediction error increasing as transition magnitude increases. These findings support the proposed preference-space control strategy within the investigated micro-milling setting and provide a foundation for future physical closed-loop validation.

papers.title: Underwrite for Collection MSME Credit LifeCycle Whitepaper
papers.abstract: Underwrite for Collection develops a proposed architecture for sustainable micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) credit across the facility lifecycle. Its central research question asks which product structures, evidence sources and proportionate interventions improve sustainable collection for defined Kenyan MSME populations, at acceptable risk, cost and customer impact. The completed research edition brings together six manuscripts across five parts. Part 1 connects the enterprise’s operating cycle, loan design and collection outcomes. Part 2a develops point-in-time evidence, entity and transaction-level cash provenance, and lifecycle features. Part 2b presents hierarchical Bayesian underwriting, uncertainty quantification, causal identification, survival and multi-state modelling, and portfolio dependence. Part 3 connects evidence to fair intervention through defined eligibility, human review, decision authority, customer agreement and follow-up. Part 4 sets out a bank-controlled research and enterprise integration architecture. Part 5 connects lifecycle cash flows to KESONIA-linked pricing, expected credit loss, capital, liquidity, asset and liability management, funds transfer pricing and risk transfer. Two reproducible worked cases accompany the manuscripts. The first follows a hypothetical MSME order through operating cash, financing, repayment timing, lender earnings, discounted recovery, guarantee settlement and an optional ring-fenced receivables structure. The second reconstructs operating cash from transaction records and follows evidence review, an authorised loan amendment, contract booking, settlement and protection re-verification. Declared assumptions, calculation code, input records and automated tests make the cases reproducible through the linked research lab. The paper distinguishes financing an operating business from financing ring-fenced receivables and explains how the two connect through repayment and collection flows. Its Kenyan governance framework incorporates the Data Protection Act 2019, the Data Protection General Regulations 2021 and relevant institutional responsibilities. Developed from a LinkedIn article series and practical questions about MSME lending, the whitepaper provides a research foundation for credit practitioners, actuaries, researchers and institutional teams. Its methods and hypothetical cases support empirical calibration, prospective evaluation and implementation planning.

papers.title: Neuromorphic control of a simulated shape-memory-alloy-driven multi-legged robot using a spiking neural network
papers.abstract: Abstract We present spiking-neural-network (SNN) reinforcement learning for autonomous locomotion control of a starfish-inspired multi-legged soft robot driven by shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators. Such robots are usually driven open loop by pre-designed periodic signals, because coordinated motion is hard to hand-design at high degrees of freedom. We replace the actor of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with an SNN: a Spiking Actor Network. The membrane potential, an internal SNN state, is reconstructed at update time from a short observation history through the current actor, rather than stored at collection time. To reduce the controller’s inference cost, we add a regularization term on the squared membrane potentials, encouraging actions from fewer spikes. In simulation the agent acquired the leg coordination needed to approach a target, and its firing patterns developed a periodicity matched to the SMA response. The resulting gait gives continuous propulsion without excessive firing. Goal error matched an ANN-actor TD3 baseline with smaller spread across seeds, and reconstruction gave the lowest goal error of the membrane-state treatments. The regularization lowered the firing rate until the estimated inference energy fell below the ANN’s.

papers.title: Forecast-Informed Shrinking-Tube Model Predictive Control for PV-Battery Building Energy Management
papers.abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage (BES) systems require coordinated operation under time-varying demand, intermittent generation, battery constraints, and imperfect forecasts. This study proposes a forecast-informed shrinking-tube model predictive control (MPC) framework for PV-battery building energy management. The method progressively tightens the admissible state-of-charge (SOC) region along the prediction horizon, retaining short-term operational flexibility while guiding the battery toward a preferred terminal range. A signal-decomposition-enhanced iTransformer is used to generate multi-step load and PV forecasts, which are supplied directly to the receding-horizon controller and evaluated in an EnergyPlus–Sinergym closed-loop environment. On the held-out forecasting set, iTransformer achieved MSE values of 0.1466 and 0.0802 for the load-side HVAC and PV series, respectively. In the five-day case study, the proposed controller reduced net purchased electricity to 152.42 kWh and cumulative SOC deviation to 55.89%·h, compared with rule-based control, standard MPC, and fixed-tube MPC. When driven by learned forecasts, the controller maintained stable closed-loop performance, with 153.85 kWh of net purchased electricity and 45.20%·h of cumulative SOC deviation. These results demonstrate the potential of horizon-dependent SOC constraint tightening for PV-battery coordination under non-ideal predictive information.

papers.title: Self-calibrating multi-fidelity active learning for microstrip patch optimization across substrates and bands
papers.abstract: Physics-aware active learning can reduce the full-wave electromagnetic (EM) cost of microstrip-patch design, but its sampling priors are commonly tuned to one substrate and band. We present an integrated self-calibrating, matching-first, physics-aware active-learning workflow for probe-fed rectangular patches, together with coarse-mesh screening and full-resolution confirmation. The online calibration estimates sampling bands from each run’s observations instead of prescribing case-specific probe locations. Under an equal budget of 37 openEMS simulations, 4 optimizers were compared on 4 substrate/frequency cases using 10 replicate seeds per case. The integrated workflow produced the lowest mean and median final objective in every case, returned a matched design in all forty runs, and was lower than the three baselines in nine of twelve exact directional Mann–Whitney comparisons after within-case Holm adjustment; six contrasts remained significant in a two-sided unpaired analysis and seven in a paired-by-seed sensitivity analysis. Multi-fidelity screening reduced mean equivalent-high-fidelity cost by 19%–46% across cases (36.9% overall) and returned a matched full-resolution design in 39 of 40 runs, although endpoint objective quality was not uniformly preserved. Nominal near-to-far-field calculations for four selected designs gave broadside directivities of 6.51–7.00 dBi and realized gains of 3.59–5.77 dBi. All 12 finer-mesh, larger-domain, and perfectly matched layer (PML) stability checks remained matched; maximum absolute directivity and realized-gain changes were 0.180 and 0.121 dB. A ten-variable E-shaped-patch case study matched all ten integrated-workflow runs. Its advantage over random search was robust to unpaired and paired-by-seed analyses; inference against unstructured radial-basis-function (RBF) surrogate search depended on the treatment of seed blocks, and the genetic comparison remained unresolved. A five-seed in-loop impedance–gain pilot produced a directionally favorable but non-significant hypervolume trend. The evidence is numerical and openEMS-based; no commercial-solver or fabricated prototype validation is claimed.

papers.title: Lower peaks, similar growth: Isolating the value and limits of artificial-intelligence-driven thermal sensation modeling for building-grid resilience under future climates
papers.abstract: Evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) in building energy control often conflate supervisory policy and occupant prediction. We present a control-isolated EnergyPlus benchmark in which three predictor-driven arms share the same supervisory logic: analytical predicted mean vote (PMV), gradient-boosted trees implemented with the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and a physics-informed neural-network variational autoencoder (PINN–VAE); a fixed-setpoint controller serves as a separate operational reference. Experiments cover five American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) climate archetypes, three 2001–2100 horizons, and Representative Concentration Pathway 8.5 (RCP8.5). The grid metric is the 95th-percentile coincident peak (CP95) of 15-minute heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning electric demand. City/weather realization accounts for 90.6% of fitted main-effect R 2 for absolute CP95 and 90.8% for warming-driven amplification; strategy identity accounts for 5.0% and 1.0%. Against the same-city, same-horizon fixed-setpoint reference, LightGBM lowers CP95 by 18–22 kilowatts (kW) per 10,000 square metres (m 2 ) on average. This is not overall superiority: its PMV-violation rate reaches 84%–94%, PINN–VAE reaches 68%–90%, and a separate annual EnergyPlus summary reaches 2,789 discomfort hours. The pooled stress-index result ( p = 0.203 ) reflects fixed design terms and hence design-induced degeneracy rather than conceptual invalidity; archetype and pathway screens alter absolute magnitudes. This applied-AI benchmark separates predictor value from its engineering application. Model comparison must combine peak and tariff effects with comfort guardrails, while long-term planning remains conditional on building stock and climate uncertainty.

papers.title: Advanced MPC-Based Bidirectional Equalization for Energy Balancing in Series-Connected EV Battery Cells
papers.abstract: Cell imbalance in series-connected battery packs, typically caused by repeated charge–discharge cycles, negatively impacts capacity, lifespan, and safety in electric vehicle (EV) applications. To address these issues, effective and reliable cell balancing is critical for maintaining battery performance and ensuring consistent energy delivery. Conventional balancing approaches often face drawbacks such as inefficient charge redistribution, limited control of energy flow, and slower response. Although bidirectional equalization strategies reduce the risks of overcharging and overdischarging, challenges remain in achieving high balancing speed, superior energy efficiency, and reduced circuit complexity. This study introduces an active bidirectional cell-to-cell equalization strategy based on a multi-winding transformer topology, where energy is directly transferred from higher-voltage to lower-voltage cells through flyback operation. A time-sharing control algorithm guided by initial state-of-charge (SoC) optimizes the sequence and prevents unnecessary transfers, while an advanced Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme further enhances dynamic regulation, efficiency, and robustness of the balancing process. The proposed system is validated using MATLAB/Simulink 2019b and real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing with the OPAL-RT OP5700 platform, demonstrating superior equalization speed and energy utilization compared to conventional techniques.
