papers.title: From Numerical Schemes to Neural Network Architectures: A Physics-Informed Framework for Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks usually incorporate differential equations primarily through the loss function, while the neural architecture itself is selected independently of the underlying numerical structure. This work develops a scheme-induced approach in which an analytically modified numerical method defines the computational architecture, while selected elements of the numerical scheme are made trainable and refined using physics-informed loss functions. The specific contribution is the formulation and systematic investigation of a class of scheme-parameterized low-fidelity physics-informed neural networks (LF-PINNs) for evolutionary PDEs. In the implementation studied here, a compact parameter network directly controls the coefficient of a generalized θ-scheme, while the implicit update is represented by a fixed number of Picard iterations. The approach is evaluated on six one-dimensional PDE benchmark configurations against conventional, hard-constrained, and adaptively weighted PINNs. The nine-parameter LF-PINN achieves competitive accuracy on several benchmark problems, while its trainable parameter remains explicitly connected to a coefficient of the underlying numerical scheme. The results also show that performance is problem-dependent and that a small number of trainable parameters does not necessarily imply lower computational cost. Stability, ablation, computational-cost, and generalization analyses further characterize the properties and limitations of the scheme-induced construction.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Control of Organoid Biofabrication with Nanoengineered Bioinks
papers.abstract: Organoids are spatiotemporal developmental systems in which tissue architecture and function emerge through dynamically coordinated interactions among cells, extracellular matrix (ECM), biochemical signals, and mechanical cues. Because these regulatory inputs vary across both space and developmental time, organoid morphogenesis requires engineering strategies that precisely control their localization, magnitude, and temporal sequence. In this review, we examine nanoengineered bioinks and bioprinting strategies as complementary approaches for coordinating the spatial organization and temporal regulation of organoid development. We discuss how bioprinting establishes cell positioning, matrix architecture, biochemical gradients, and vascular-like structures within three-dimensional (3D) organoid models. We then examine how nanoengineered bioinks control factor release, matrix remodeling, mechanical evolution, and reciprocal cell-matrix interactions over time. Applications in brain, tumor, cardiac, skeletal muscle, and intestinal organoids illustrate how these design principles support tissue-specific patterning, multicellular interactions, and functional maturation. Finally, we highlight future directions for advancing organoid bioprinting toward predictive and developmentally responsive platforms, including adaptive bioinks, longitudinal monitoring, and data-guided optimization.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Adaptive Controllers for Resilient Unmanned Aerial and Unmanned Ground Vehicles Cooperative Systems: A Mini Review
papers.abstract: Teams of cooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are becoming crucial in scenarios where their complementary mobility, sensing capabilities, endurance, and physical interaction are beneficial. While UAVs offer fast aerial inspection and flexible perspectives, UGVs ensure large payloads, extended operation time, and the ability to intervene from ground level. Nonetheless, reliable UAV–UGV cooperation is challenging due to different dynamics, occasional communication, limited computational power, uncertain environments, and severe constraints on energy. This updated mini-review aims to bring together state-of-the-art and peer-reviewed research on using artificial intelligence (AI) for enhancing adaptive controllers in air-ground cooperation problems. This paper addresses four interconnected topics: learning-enabled control, model predictive and hybrid AI-model predictive control controllers, resilient coordination considering limited communication, and energy-conscious mission planning. As opposed to UAV–UGV surveys, this paper highlights the control-related aspects of air-ground cooperation, which include learning policies, constraint satisfaction, task allocation, degraded communication-based re-planning, and energy-dependent rendezvous. The revision significantly improves the process of selecting relevant literature, eliminates claims on benchmarks without evidence, updates unverified citations or references unrelated to the work, and produces publication-quality graphics. Ultimately, the review suggests that robust implementation would require explainable AI, rigorous sim-to-real transfer techniques, standardization of heterogeneous benchmarks, and efficient lightweight algorithms suitable for limited resources.

papers.title: SkinSense: Dermatological Screening and Skin-Care Advisory System
papers.abstract: Access to dermatological assessment in many regions is limited less by the availability of imaging than by the availability of trained specialists, and the resulting delay affects precisely those lesions for which early attention matters most. Most reported systems terminate at a single classification score, give no indication of how ambiguous that score is, and provide the end user with no actionable guidance. This paper describes SkinSense, a web-deployed educational screening and preventive advisory system joining seven-class lesion classification with EfficientNetV2, lesion delineation with U-Net, entropy-based uncertainty quantification, Grad-CAM visual attribution, heuristic risk banding, disease-specific preventive guidance and a locally hosted retrieval-based educational assistant inside one authenticated request pipeline built on FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite and a React front end. Classification is trained and evaluated on 10,013 de-duplicated ISIC 2018 Task 3 images under a fixed 7,009 / 1,502 / 1,502 partition whose test portion is withheld from every design and tuning decision. On that partition the baseline network records 52.86% accuracy, 46.49% balanced accuracy, 32.30% macro F1, 58.65% weighted F1 and 84.57% ROC-AUC; a compute-constrained improved configuration reaches 61.65% accuracy, 52.06% balanced accuracy and 39.81% macro F1. The limited-training U-Net attains a Dice coefficient of 67.68%, an IoU of 53.29% and pixel accuracy of 86.85%. A variational-autoencoder augmentation trial using thirty generated minority-class images reduced macro F1 to 16.68% and is reported as a negative result rather than suppressed. The contribution claimed is the integration itself — an uncertainty-gated advisory workflow with transparent reporting — not a new accuracy record. The system is explicitly educational and does not perform clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Developing computational thinking in teacher education: a brief experience with coding, robotics, and machine learning
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examines post-intervention self-reported outcomes associated with a short intervention designed to introduce coding, educational robotics, and introductory concepts of machine learning into initial teacher education for Primary Education. The proposal is grounded in Papert’s principles and the Creative and Computational Problem Solving model, combining active learning methodologies with accessible technologies. A quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent control group was employed. A total of 144 first-year students from three Spanish universities participated (105 in the experimental group and 39 in the control group). The intervention consisted of a two-hour workshop with hands-on stations and technological challenges, designed as a feasible microintervention within regular teacher education contexts. Assessment was carried out through an ad hoc questionnaire focused on three dimensions: knowledge of programming and machine learning, block-based programming and game engines, and active learning, all assessed through self-reported perceptions. The results showed statistically significant post-intervention differences in favor of the experimental group, with a small effect size for knowledge of programming and machine learning and large effect sizes for block-based programming and game engines and active learning. Item-level analyses revealed that favorable overall perceptions coexisted with lower self-reported familiarity in specific technical areas, particularly machine learning, prior experience with block-based programming, and programming in game engines. Three exploratory response profiles were also identified: reluctant, intermediate, and enthusiastic. The findings suggest that well-structured microinterventions may support higher self-reported knowledge of programming and machine learning, greater familiarity with block-based programming and game engines, and more positive perceptions of active learning in teacher education.

papers.title: Beyond Permeability Prediction: Machine Learning for Gas-Separation Membranes from Data Curation to Experimentally Validated Discovery
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is transforming gas-separation membrane research, yet high retrospective accuracy does not necessarily translate into experimentally viable or process-relevant materials. This review reframes the field around the evidence chain required to convert a membrane record into a defensible discovery decision. Across polymers, metal–organic and covalent organic frameworks, mixed-matrix membranes, carbon molecular sieves, and two-dimensional systems, we critically examine data curation, physics-aligned representation, multitask and multi-fidelity learning, uncertainty quantification, inverse design, and prospective validation. We introduce a five-level evidence framework spanning retrospective interpolation, domain-disjoint generalization, physics or simulation confirmation, prospective membrane validation, and deployment-relevant testing. We further propose a contextualized observation unit that binds chemical identity to membrane state, fabrication history, feed composition, operating conditions, time, protocol, and provenance, thereby exposing leakage and structural uncertainty hidden by conventional datasets. Our analysis shows that ML has demonstrably accelerated data completion, simulation, and candidate prioritization, whereas evidence for routinely discovering manufacturable, durable, mixed-gas-performing membranes remains limited and concentrated in polymer studies. To close this gap, we develop a constrained, uncertainty-aware closed-loop architecture that treats feasibility and fabrication failures as learnable outcomes, couples acquisition to multiscale process utility, and advances candidates through staged experimental fidelities. A minimum reporting standard and measurable research priorities are provided. Together, these contributions propose “decision-grade ML” as an emerging framework for evaluating machine learning in membrane science: models should know their applicability domain, preserve physical context, propose feasible experiments, quantify uncertainty under domain shift, and demonstrate value under the conditions of intended membrane use rather than merely reproduce familiar labels or idealized proxies.

papers.title: Hybrid PINN–SSF Framework for Mode-Locked Fiber Laser Simulation: Comparative Assessment with SSF and FDM
papers.abstract: Abstract Simulating intracavity pulse evolution in mode-locked fiber lasers (MLFLs) requires solving the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE), typically via the split-step Fourier (SSF) or finite-difference (FDM) methods, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as a mesh-free alternative. Yet a quantitative benchmark of all three within a unified dissipative cavity model remains absent. Here we adopt a hybrid PINN-SSF strategy to overcome the limitations of standalone PINNs in gain-saturated dynamics, and compare its performance against SSF and FDM over fifty consecutive round trips. The results reveal distinct error-accumulation behaviors: Within the tested cavity configuration, SSF serves as the numerical reference supported by discretization-refinement tests; FDM exhibits increasing global field differences during repeated cavity propagation while retaining visible late-stage sideband-like structures; the hybrid PINN-SSF exhibits earlier temporal localization during the initial stage, yet suffers from high-frequency spectral degradation and a 50% energy drift from 10 pJ to approximately 5 pJ over 50 round trips, despite achieving a lower mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.275% versus 2.092% relative to SSF. In conclusion, within the tested ring-cavity configuration and under the investigated parameter set, SSF remains optimal for long-term high-fidelity modeling, FDM suits sideband-resolved analysis with adequate resolution, and the hybrid PINN-SSF, while promising for early-stage prediction, still requires improved stationary dissipative balance for extended cavity simulations.

papers.title: Optimal verification planning for the Large Lenslet Array Magellan Spectrograph
papers.abstract: For complex astronomical systems, verification must be carried out under significant programmatic constraints, and the risk of running over-schedule and over-budget is significant. Verification planning is the problem of deciding how to allocate resources in this process, to achieve a desired level of confidence in system performance. Traditional methods of verification planning, often based on heuristics or historical approaches, may result in too many resources spent on tests which do not raise the confidence of performance sufficiently. We leverage advancements in uncertainty quantification and experimental design to determine verification test plans that minimize effort and maximize certainty of system performance. A systems engineering methodology for goal-oriented simulation-based optimal Bayesian experimental design is presented. This approach is demonstrated for verification of the Large Lenslet Array Magellan Spectrograph (LLAMAS), a fiber-fed spectrograph developed for the Magellan Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory at the MIT Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research. For a complex science system with ∼250 optical components, verification is essential for ensuring confidence in the system’s performance. A retrospective analysis of the sensitivity verification for LLAMAS shows that optimized plans can reduce testbed time by 94% without a loss in performance uncertainty reduction compared with the historical AI&T approach. These optimized plans are compared with the historical outcomes of V&V for LLAMAS to show that they lead to greater uncertainty reduction with a confidence of over 90%.

papers.title: AI-DRIVEN OPTIMIZATION OF A SMARTPHONE-BASED COLORIMETRIC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS DETERMINATION OF MULTIPLE HEAVY METAL IONS IN ENVIRONMENTAL WATER OF BABIL GOVERNORATE, IRAQ
papers.abstract: Copper, lead, cadmium, mercury, chromium, zinc and nickel reach rivers, irrigation canals and groundwater from industrial effluents, agricultural drainage, urban wastewater and corroding distribution pipes, and several of them are harmful at microgram-per-litre levels. Their routine determination still depends on atomic absorption and inductively coupled plasma instruments, which are expensive, need trained operators and are rarely available near the sampling site. This research plan describes a low-cost method in which a six-reagent chromogenic array (4-(2-pyridylazo)resorcinol, Zincon, micellar dithizone, 1,5-diphenylcarbazide, dimethylglyoxime and xylenol orange) is prepared in a 96-well microplate and photographed with a smartphone inside a closed enclosure with controlled LED lighting. Color values will be extracted from every well in the RGB, HSV, HSL and CIELAB spaces after correction against a reference card. Reaction pH, reagent concentration, reaction time and sample volume will be screened with a Box–Behnken design and refined by Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization. Multiple linear regression, partial least squares, random forest, support vector regression and artificial neural network models will be trained on synthetic multi-metal mixtures to predict the seven concentrations at the same time, and they will be compared by nested cross-validation and an external test set using the root mean square error, mean absolute error and coefficient of determination. The selected procedure will be validated following ICH Q2(R2) and Eurachem guidance for linearity, detection and quantification limits, precision, recovery, selectivity, interference and robustness, and then applied to surface, well and tap water from Babil Governorate, Republic of Iraq, with ICP-MS as the reference method. The expected result is a portable procedure that screens seven metals in one run of about 25 minutes, at a small fraction of the cost of instrumental analysis.

papers.title: Macroscopic–microscopic information fusion: a novel reliable bearing diagnosis method with physical embedding and uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Lots of multimodal fusion models have been extensively applied in bearing fault diagnosis. However, they overlook the fusion uncertainty among different modalities and the fine-grained selection of fault information within a single modality. To this end, a novel reliable multimodal diagnosis framework named macroscopic–microscopic information fusion (MMIF) is developed. In MMIF, the microscopic physical embedding selection mechanism is first proposed to estimate the weight corresponding to different components of single modality, thereby enhancing the representation of intrinsic fault features. Subsequently, a new macroscopic uncertainty quantification scheme with D-S evidence theory is constructed to adaptively solve the uncertainty probability of each whole modality, achieving the fusion of multi-source monitoring signals. Besides, the joint optimization strategy with local weight regularization and global evidence calibration is designed to guarantee the effectiveness of the MMIF framework. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate on both vibration and current modalities that the proposed MMIF outperforms several state-of-the-art diagnosis methods. Source code is available at https://github.com/PHM-QQteam/MMIF .

papers.title: Per-Class Conformal Risk Control for Multi-Label ECG Classification: Achieving Clinically-Justified False Negative Rate Guarantees
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) classifiers require uncertainty procedures that address class-specific clinical risk in intrinsically multi-label data. Approach: We propose per-class risk-controlling prediction sets for multi-label ECG classification. For each diagnostic class, binary false-negative-rate (FNR) loss is calibrated with a one-sided exact-binomial upper confidence bound. The nine disease-specific targets are controlled simultaneously at 95% family-wise confidence using Bonferroni allocation. The final operating threshold is the more inclusive of the exact-binomial threshold and a conservative reference threshold derived from a concentration bound; this safeguard uses calibration data only and cannot weaken the exact guarantee. Main results: We evaluated the method on PTB-XL (21,388 retained recordings) and Chapman-Shaoxing (10,199 retained recordings), using a patient-disjoint PTB-XL split and fitting-partition-only normalisation. The proposed method met all 9/9 prespecified disease-specific FNR targets on held-out test sets and produced non-vacuous simultaneous exact-binomial guarantees for all nine targets; uniform standard conformal prediction met 5/9. Test FNR was 0.0% for myocardial infarction (exact 95% upper bound 0.35%, at 80.3% FPR), 1.0% for ST/T changes, and 0.3% for atrial fibrillation; the high-sensitivity operating point is purchased with substantially reduced specificity. Under PTB-XL-to-Chapman shift, macro class coverage fell from 94.3% to 45.5%, demonstrating that the guarantees do not transport without local recalibration. Significance: Exact-binomial per-class risk control provides a transparent high-sensitivity operating point for ECG triage while making its specificity, prediction-set-size, calibration-support, and exchangeability limitations explicit. .

papers.title: Hiccup: A Resource-Efficient Automated Platform for High-Performance Global Neural Network Potentials Training
papers.abstract: Abstract Neural network potentials (NNPs) enable atomistic simulations with near-first-principles accuracy at greatly reduced cost, yet the construction of specialized high-accuracy NNPs for complex systems remains limited by expert-dependent workflows and the challenge of achieving high accuracy and robust generalization under limited computational budgets. Here we present Hiccup, a resource-efficient automated platform for training high-performance global NNPs. Hiccup leverages prior guidance from universal NNPs to overcome the cold-start bottleneck of active learning, and integrates this initialization with hierarchical genetic algorithm–molecular dynamics (GA–MD) sampling to enable both broad configurational exploration and targeted refinement of low-energy basins. Building on these algorithmic advances, the platform further implements an asynchronous submit-and-forget scheduling mechanism that minimizes resource idling by overlapping first-principles labeling with subsequent sampling, training, and evaluation on the GPU. We demonstrate the application and efficiency of Hiccup using the Cu–Y–O ternary system as a case study. The resulting system-specific NNP achieves near-first-principles accuracy in static predictions and exhibits robust long-time dynamical fidelity across a broad thermodynamic range. These results establish Hiccup as a practical and scalable infrastructure for automated construction of high-quality interatomic potentials for chemically complex systems.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of nuclear materials under irradiation extremes: thermal-mechanical performance, qualification challenges, and future research directions
papers.abstract: This review examines additive manufacturing (AM) of nuclear materials. Three core advantages of AM for nuclear reactor components are identified: high geometric complexity, short lead times, and tunable microstructures. Five mainstream AM technologies are reviewed: laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), directed energy deposition (DED), electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and binder jetting. Focusing on four material classes (austenitic and ferritic-martensitic steels, oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) alloys, refractory metals and plasma-facing materials, and silicon carbide composites), the review establishes process–structure–property–performance (PSPP) relationships. The core emphasis is on thermomechanical behavior under extreme operating conditions: temperatures up to 1,000 °C (Generation IV reactors), transient heat fluxes exceeding 10 MW m -2 (fusion devices), and neutron irradiation up to 200 displacements per atom (dpa). AM-specific irradiation failure mechanisms are analyzed. Four critical unresolved problems are identified: (i) thermal stability of AM-specific dislocation structures under service conditions, (ii) conflicting reports on irradiation swelling resistance between AM and wrought alloys, (iii) absence of standardized qualification pathways, and (iv) limited neutron irradiation data, with existing data restricted to doses below 10 dpa. Finally, the review highlights knowledge gaps concerning synergistic effects among irradiation, corrosion, and thermomechanical loading and proposes prioritized directions for future research.

papers.title: Periodic–Kink, Lump, and Rogue Waves with Parameter Discovery in an Integrable Model: Bilinear and Physics-Informed Neural-Network Approaches
papers.abstract: This research investigates nonlinear wave dynamics of the integrable (3+1)-dimensional extended Bogoyavlensky- Konopelchenko equation, which models the interaction of a Riemann wave and a long wave in fluid dynamics. The equation has important applications in the modeling of shallow water waves, ion acoustic waves, and the propagation of fluids. Initially, we employ Hirota’s bilinear framework with symbolic single-hidden-layer neural-network architectures, referred to as bilinear neural networks (BNNs), and prescribed analytical activation functions to construct complex wave structures, including periodic–kink waves, M-lumps, lump–kink interactions, and modulated lump solutions. A Jacobielliptic activation function is employed within the symbolic BNN ansatz to construct and investigate rogue-wave solutions. In the second phase, an enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), equipped with a global adaptive activation function and residual-based attention, is introduced for physics-informed solution approximation and inverse parameter identification. The proposed PINN accurately reproduces the periodic–kink, M-lump, and lump–kink dynamics, showing good agreement with the analytical solutions and low error metrics, while the comparative analysis highlights the complementary strengths and limitations of the analytical and physics-informed numerical approaches. The framework also exhibits good stability in recovering nonlinear coefficients from noisy data, demonstrating its potential for parameter discovery. The results demonstrate that combining BNN-based exact solution construction with enhanced PINN-based numerical forward and inverse modeling provides a versatile framework for nonlinear wave analysis and the investigation of complex wave phenomena in applied mathematics and nonlinear physics.

papers.title: FLARE: Analytical uncertainty quantification and linear-nonlinear decomposition for interpretable clinical risk prediction
papers.abstract: In clinical risk prediction, accurate estimation of predictive uncertainty and transparent interpretation of model behaviour are as important as discrimination performance. While logistic regression supports statistical inference, its ability to capture nonlinear relationships is limited. Kernel-based, tree-based, and deep learning methods can accommodate nonlinear effects but generally do not provide closed-form uncertainty quantification, parametric inference, or analytical decomposition of variable effects into linear and nonlinear components. Moreover, these methods fall short in constructing uncertainty profiles at the individual patient and risk group levels. Fourier–Laplace Analytical Risk Estimation (FLARE) is presented as a unified framework for nonlinear clinical risk modelling and analytical uncertainty quantification. FLARE combines Orthogonal Random Fourier Features with a Laplace approximation to estimate uncertainty arising from model parameters, kernel hyperparameters, and their interaction. The framework provides (i) closed-form prediction uncertainty at the patient level, (ii) Wald tests, confidence intervals, and odds ratios through Jacobian-based projection, (iii) decomposition of variable effects into linear and nonlinear components via path-dependent gradient analysis, and (iv) analytical Hessian-based patient-specific interaction analysis within a single model. FLARE was evaluated on four real-world clinical datasets and two synthetic datasets. Under linear data-generating conditions, FLARE produced results functionally equivalent to logistic regression, while yielding improved predictive performance in nonlinear settings. Analytical confidence intervals achieved coverage close to nominal levels, and attribution patterns showed strong agreement with SHAP-based explanations. In the FLChain cohort, interactions undetectable at the population level were found to be substantially amplified in specific high-risk patients, with certain covariate pairs exhibiting markedly stronger effects locally than at the population mean. FLARE integrates the inferential transparency of classical statistical models with the representational power of nonlinear methods within a single analytical framework. The method provides closed-form uncertainty estimates, interpretable linear–nonlinear effect decomposition, and patient-level interaction assessment, facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of model behaviour in clinical prediction settings.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Mineral Prospectivity Mapping with Positive-Unlabeled Learning and Conformal Calibration: Ni Mineralization in the Yilgarn Craton
papers.abstract: Abstract Mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) supports exploration targeting, yet most machine learning approaches emphasize point probabilities with limited uncertainty quantification or coverage guarantees. Regional MPM faces incomplete deposit labels from biased exploration, spatial autocorrelation invalidating random cross-validation, and limited decision-relevant guidance linking probability surfaces to exploration priorities. This study develops a framework that combines positive-unlabeled learning, nested spatial block cross-validation, bootstrap ensemble uncertainty, and cross-conformal calibration, and converts the resulting signals into five priority zones defined by lift-based percentile thresholds and a 30% relative interquartile range ( $$\rho _{\text {IQR}}$$ ρ IQR ) cut-off. On the Yilgarn Craton, Western Australia (70,200 grid cells at 5 km resolution, 818 cells containing at least one known Ni deposit location, a 1.17% positive rate), the framework uses nested fivefold spatial block cross-validation with 50 km blocks informed by an empirical variogram. XGBoost and a BaggingPU-XGBoost variant achieve nearly identical outer test PR-AUC of 0.195 and 0.194 and ROC-AUC of 0.911, and the Excluded zone removes 9% of the positive cells at empirical coverage exceeding the 85% nominal target. BaggingPU-XGBoost produces more stable high-probability predictions, with median $$\rho _{\text {IQR}}$$ ρ IQR of 18% in the top 1% of bootstrap mean probabilities compared with 48% for XGBoost. This stability advantage shifts deposits into a more populated Immediate zone, so the combined Immediate and Priority zones of BaggingPU-XGBoost capture 33% of the positive cells compared with 23% for XGBoost. The framework provides an uncertainty-informed prioritization for MPM workflows in which discovery efficiency must be balanced against costs and investment risks.

papers.title: Multicenter Validation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Myopia Progression Across School‐Based Screening and Optical Intervention Settings in Chinese Children and Adolescents
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of myopia progression is critical for personalized clinical decision‐making. This study aimed to develop machine‐learning models leveraging ocular biometric parameters to predict myopia status, rapid progression, and spherical equivalent (SE) using multicenter data from 40 445 individuals across 10 hospitals. Data from one hospital were used for training and internal validation, while the remaining data were used for external validation. Models (i.e., XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, K‐Nearest Neighbors, Naive Bayes, and FT‐Transformer) were evaluated using 12 clinical variables as input features, with hyperparameters automatically optimized via Bayesian optimization. In external validation, the best‐performing models in the school‐based screening group were Logistic Regression for myopia status (AUROC = 0.860) and rapid progression (AUROC = 0.620), and Gradient Boosting for SE prediction ( R 2 = 0.596). In the optical interventions group, XGBoost, Extra Trees, and FT‐Transformer performed best for myopia status (AUROC = 0.969), rapid progression (AUROC = 0.663), and SE prediction ( R 2 = 0.830), respectively. Our study demonstrates accurate prediction of myopia trajectories across school‐based screening and optical intervention settings, enabling clinically precise risk stratification and personalized management to inform timely interventions and help mitigate the escalating global myopia burden.

papers.title: Integrating model predictive control and reinforcement learning for robust Six-DOF AUV trajectory tracking
papers.abstract: To address model uncertainties, ocean-current disturbances, and real-time control requirements in six-degree-of-freedom AUV trajectory tracking, this paper proposes a residual-learning-enhanced MPC–PID hierarchical control framework. An outer-loop kinematic model predictive controller generates constraint-aware velocity references, while an inner-loop inverse-dynamics PID controller provides nominal dynamic compensation and fast velocity tracking. A reinforcement-learning-based compensator generates bounded residual actions to mitigate tracking errors caused by unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances without replacing the model-based controller. The proposed method is evaluated on a six-degree-of-freedom AUV simulation platform using three representative trajectories under nominal and random ocean-current conditions. Compared with representative model-based and learning-based controllers, RLMPC achieves a better overall trade-off among position tracking, attitude stability, disturbance rejection, control effort, and actuator constraint satisfaction. An additional comparison with MPC–PID–DOB shows that conventional observer-based compensation improves the robustness of MPC–PID, whereas residual learning provides more balanced performance across the tested scenarios. Under random disturbances, RLMPC reduces position and attitude tracking errors by up to 36.2% and 47.1%, respectively, relative to MPC–PID. The controller also maintains millisecond-level computation time, demonstrating its real-time computational feasibility.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Action-Conditioned Latent World Models for Risk-Aware Thermal Planning in 5G Radio Access Infrastructure-Reproducibility Package
papers.abstract: Reproducibility package for the article "Physics-Guided Action-Conditioned Latent World Models for Risk-Aware Thermal Planning in 5G Radio Access Infrastructure" by J. O. Aji, P. Xiao and M. Shojafar (submitted to IEEE Access, 2026). OverviewThe package reproduces every synthetic-benchmark result in the paper: forecasting accuracy and calibration (Tables III, A1–A2; Figs. 3–4), hidden-state reconstruction (Fig. 5), counterfactual planning, ablations and paired statistics (Tables IV–V; Figs. 6–7), and site heterogeneity (Table VI). PG-WM embeds a two-node resistance–capacitance (RC) thermal transition with history-conditioned bounded parameters in an action-conditioned latent world model, adds a bounded recurrent residual and a heteroscedastic Gaussian head, and drives a risk-aware planner evaluated against simulator ground truth. Contents1. simulator/ – two-node RC digital twin of 5G RAN site thermal dynamics (Eqs. 1–5) with ambient, load, solar and outage drivers, cooling-health degradation, sensor faults (stuck-at, drift, spikes) and an operator-like behaviour policy.2. models/ – PG-WM and six baselines: persistence, nominal Physics-RC, Ridge-ARX, XGBoost, LSTM and GRU-WM.3. planning/ – 20-plan action set, upper-confidence feasibility test (z = 1.645), operating-cost model, simulator replay, regret and violation metrics (Eqs. 11–13).4. configs/ – all training and evaluation settings (Table I), seeds 0, 1, 2.5. data/synthetic/ – 48 in-distribution sites (75 days) and 20 out-of-distribution sites (30 days, +2.0 °C ambient, 1.8× degradation) at 5-min resolution (1,209,600 records), per-site simulator parameters (Table II) and the site split (31 train / 6 validation / 11 test).6. checkpoints/ – trained LSTM, GRU-WM and PG-WM models for seeds 0–2.7. logs/ablations/ – training logs for the physics-off and action-off variants.8. results/ – site-level forecasting metrics, decision-averaged planning summaries and paired-test outputs.9. figures/ – scripts and source data for all figures. How to reproduce(1) Install the dependencies in requirements.txt. (2) Regenerate the synthetic data, or use data/synthetic directly. (3) Train each model for seeds 0, 1 and 2. (4) Run the forecasting evaluation on the test and OOD splits. (5) Run the planning evaluation on the fixed 400 decision states per split. (6) Regenerate the figures. Exact commands are in README.md. Integrity checksCorrect outputs satisfy: (a) thousands of evaluation windows per site (about 3,600 per ID test site and 1,440 per OOD site at a 30-min stride); (b) RMSE_all² equals the mean of the twelve squared horizon RMSEs in every row; (c) 400 decision states × 3 seeds = 1,200 paired decisions per split, shared by all models. Ground-truth columns prefixed GT_ are for evaluation only and must never be model inputs. Known limitationsFrozen prediction tensors from the original runs were not archived. The archived RMSE_h12 field duplicates RMSE_all; 60-min RMSE was regenerated for the three neural models. End-to-end equivalence between reloaded checkpoints and archived predictions has not yet been demonstrated. All dynamics data are synthetic. Field telemetryThe operator telemetry (250 sites, 12,000 records) used for the steady-state consistency check in Section VIII is proprietary to the network operator and is not included. Aggregated results are provided; access to the underlying records may be requested from the corresponding author, subject to the operator's approval. LicencesCode: MIT. papers.title: Enhancing nursing students’ learning of nutrition through podcasting: An active approach for Generation Z students in Morocco
papers.abstract: Background Student-generated video podcasting may support active learning in nursing education, but evidence from low- and middle-income settings remains limited. Material and Methods This two-academic-year, non-randomized consecutive-cohort study was conducted at the Taza annex of the Higher Institute of Nursing and Health Techniques, Fes, Morocco. The 2024-2025 cohort (n = 135) completed a collaborative student-generated video-podcasting activity for the therapeutic diets unit, involving group content research, script preparation, recording, presentation, peer viewing, and supervised discussion, whereas the 2025-2026 cohort (n = 119) received traditional instruction. In both cohorts, the nutrition unit was taught and assessed first, followed by the therapeutic diets unit. Each unit was evaluated by an end-of-unit written examination graded on a 10-point scale, and the overall module grade was the mean of the two unit scores. The nutrition score therefore preceded the therapeutic-diets intervention and was used as a pre-intervention academic comparator. The therapeutic-diets written examinations used different questions across academic years but assessed the same construct and learning objectives; item difficulty indices were used to minimize differences in examination difficulty. Welch t-tests and an ANCOVA model adjusted for nutrition score were used. Results Cohorts were comparable for gender, program, age, and pre-intervention nutrition score (6.16 ± 1.37 vs. 6.18 ± 1.35; p = 0.907). The intervention cohort achieved a higher therapeutic-diets written examination score than the traditional cohort (7.20 ± 1.21 vs. 6.24 ± 1.30; mean difference = 0.96, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.27; p < 0.001; d = 0.77). The adjusted mean difference was 0.97 points (95% CI 0.69 to 1.25; p < 0.001). Satisfaction was favorable, but internal consistency was below the conventional 0.70 threshold (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.69), so item-level interpretation was retained. Conclusions The implemented video-based collaborative learning activity was associated with a higher therapeutic-diets written examination score. Because the intervention was multicomponent and cohorts were not randomized, the observed association cannot be attributed specifically to video podcasting. Prospective controlled replication using a common or item-banked examination is needed.

papers.title: Learning-based decoupled CVT-MPC for plug-in hybrid electric vehicles: An ANFIS-enabled approach
papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) enables real-time energy management for plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) by utilizing future driving information. However, conventional MPC mainly optimizes power split and overlooks engine operating point optimization. Although incorporating continuously variable transmission (CVT) ratio optimization can improve engine efficiency, it increases the dimension of the online optimization problem. To overcome this limitation, a learning-based decoupled CVT–MPC energy management strategy is proposed. First, two-dimensional dynamic programming (2D-DP) is employed to jointly optimize the SOC trajectory, power split, and CVT ratio. An adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) is then trained to learn the optimal CVT control policy and establish the mapping between vehicle operating conditions and the optimal transmission ratio. During online operation, the ANFIS policy determines the CVT ratio, after which PMP-based receding-horizon optimization within the MPC framework allocates engine and motor power using a 10-s demand preview and the corresponding SOC reference. This hierarchical implementation transfers the coupled 2D-DP control results to the online controller while avoiding joint online optimization of the CVT ratio and power split. The proposed strategy is evaluated under a representative driving cycle generated in VISSIM and compared with rule-based (RB), dynamic programming (DP), and 2D-DP strategies. Results show that the proposed method effectively concentrates engine operating points near the Optimal Efficiency Line (OEL). The ANFIS model achieves CVT-ratio RMSEs of 0.057 and 0.067 on the testing and checking datasets, respectively. After correcting the terminal-SOC difference, the equivalent fuel consumption is 2.83 L/100 km, representing a reduction of 17.7% compared with the RB strategy. The proposed strategy provides an effective solution for improving engine efficiency and fuel economy in CVT-based PHEVs.

papers.title: Research on Improved MPC-Based Control Strategies for PEMFC Under Low-Temperature and Normal Temperature Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: In polar marine equipment, proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are subject to two canonical regimes—low-temperature cold start and normal temperature load operation—under which standard model predictive control (MPC) manifests fundamentally distinct deficiencies. During cold start, the MPC reference trajectory fails to track the direction of maximum heat generation in real time; during normal temperature load operation, MPC rests on a deterministic prediction model and is therefore incapable of quantifying the prediction uncertainty arising from model mismatch. To overcome these limitations, we embedded two auxiliary mechanisms within the MPC architecture: an extremum-seeking control (ESC) algorithm that furnishes MPC with a maximum power reference trajectory under low-temperature conditions, and sparse variational Bayesian learning (SVB) that equips MPC with probabilistic prediction capability under normal temperature conditions. Crucially, both enhancements retain the receding-horizon optimization structure of the baseline MPC. A lumped-parameter PEMFC model was developed in MATLAB (R2025b) and validated against data taken from the literature for the low-temperature regime and against a 1 kW stack experiment for the normal temperature regime. The results demonstrate that, under the −10 °C cold start condition, ESC-MPC shortens the startup time to 19.8 s—a 24.5% reduction relative to standard MPC and a 44.4% reduction relative to optimal constant current density (CCD) control—while the peak ice volume fraction attains 61%, remaining below the safety threshold. Under the 25 °C load-step condition, SVB-MPC attenuates the voltage overshoot by 51.2% relative to PID and by 34.1% relative to standard MPC, achieves zero steady-state error in temperature regulation, and reduces the settling time by 34.7% compared with standard MPC. Collectively, these findings establish that configuring regime-specific auxiliary mechanisms within the MPC framework effectively compensates for the deficiencies of standard MPC under both operating regimes, thereby offering a viable pathway toward the reliable application of PEMFC in extreme polar environments and clean energy systems in coastal areas.

papers.title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
papers.abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV ⋅ h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations.

papers.title: Topology-regulated load transfer mechanisms and mechanical performance of sheet-based TPMS titanium scaffolds
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide a route to control stiffness while retaining pore space, but quantitative links among topology, load transfer, and mechanical response remain limited. This study establishes a topology-load transfer-mechanical response framework by integrating quasi-static compression experiments, Digital Image Correlation, and validated finite element analysis on representative Triply Periodic Minimal Surface titanium scaffolds. The Gyroid-Sheet scaffold exhibits a topology-regulated progressive instability-restabilization deformation mode, distinctly different from the conventional lattice structures exhibiting plateau-dominated yielding behavior. GS20 exhibited experimental Young's modulus and yield strength of 2.26 GPa and 49.6 MPa, whereas FEA predicted 2.68 GPa and 65.43 MPa; therefore, simulations were used only for comparative interpretation. Numerically, its normalized modulus and strength were 13.40 GPa and 327.15 MPa, approximately 36% and 20% higher than PS20, respectively, indicating superior predicted material utilization under identical idealized conditions rather than experimentally validated cross-topology mechanical properties for fabricated TPMS scaffolds. Gibson-Ashby analysis suggests that the Gyroid-Sheet topology retains mechanical efficiency as relative density decreases. A multiscale framework combining elastic anisotropy, principal-stress streamlines, and strain-energy density was then used to interpret how topology governs load transfer and localized mechanical response patterns. The Gyroid-Sheet structure exhibits a near-isotropic elastic response (Zener index = 1.13), along with a higher proportion of stress streamline segments with deflection angle θ < 15° (5.19%) and local turning angle φ < 15° (39.96%), indicating enhanced directional coherence and spatial continuity of load transfer paths. G GS20 testing and comparative simulations suggest that continuous sheet topology promotes load-transfer continuity, material utilization, and resistance to localized energy concentration. These characteristics may support stiffness regulation and load sharing while preserving interconnected pore space for potential fluid and tissue access. The proposed mechanics-based framework therefore provides a basis for screening orthopedic scaffold architectures, although broader experimental validation remains necessary.

papers.title: Posterior sampling of word embeddings
papers.abstract: Abstract We study Bayesian inference for probabilistic word embedding models, including skip-gram with negative sampling (SGNS) and continuous bag-of-words (CBoW). These models are widely used for inference, but their posteriors are non-identifiable under general linear transformations, which prevents meaningful Bayesian uncertainty quantification. We provide a simple and principled identifiability constraint that yields a well-defined posterior without altering the data model. Building on this, we develop scalable, fully Bayesian posterior sampling algorithms for SGNS and CBoW using Pólya–Gamma augmentation. Our block Gibbs samplers yield exact samples from the posterior and scale well to large corpora due to their straightforward parallelisation. We discuss the efficient implementation of the Gibbs sampler, and provide a fast TensorFlow reference implementation. In a combination of simulations and empirical experiments, we demonstrate that the sampler is both accurate and computationally efficient. It matches the accuracy of NUTS-HMC at a fraction of the computational cost and avoids the variance underestimation of mean-field variational inference. On large real datasets, we show that posterior means yield improved predictive performance, while posterior credible intervals provide meaningful uncertainty quantification for semantic similarity.

papers.title: Managing Severe Proximal Femoral Fibrous Dysplasia in a Young Adult Using Hemiarthroplasty in a Resource-Constrained Healthcare System: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Fibrous dysplasia of the proximal femur may lead to progressive deformity, pain, and pathological fractures, with shepherd's crook deformity representing one of its most severe manifestations.Although valgus osteotomy with intramedullary fixation is considered the preferred surgical treatment, extensive bone destruction and limited healthcare resources may preclude conventional reconstruction.We present a case of severe proximal femoral fibrous dysplasia successfully managed with bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty in a resource-constrained healthcare setting.A 25-year-old man presented with progressive left hip pain, severe proximal femoral deformity, and impaired ambulation.Radiographic evaluation demonstrated lateral bowing of the proximal femur, while histopathological examination following core biopsy confirmed fibrous dysplasia.Internal fixation using an intramedullary nail was initially planned; however, intraoperative findings revealed extensive fibro-osseous replacement, severely compromised bone quality, and inadequate cortical support, making stable fixation technically impossible.Because more complex reconstructive procedures were not covered by the national health insurance system, a bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty, augmented with plate fixation of the osteotomized fragments, was performed as a salvage procedure.The postoperative course was uneventful, with marked pain relief, improved gait, and satisfactory functional recovery at 10 months of follow-up (Oxford Hip Score 34/48).Conventional fixation for shepherd's crook deformity requires adequate residual cortical bone to achieve stable implant fixation.In cases with extensive cortical destruction and bone stock too thin to support reliable press-fit fixation, cemented hemiarthroplasty may represent a practical alternative.Preservation of the native acetabulum may also reduce postoperative instability while providing satisfactory functional outcomes.Bipolar cemented hemiarthroplasty may be an effective salvage option for selected patients with severe proximal femoral fibrous dysplasia when conventional fixation is technically unfeasible, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare systems.

papers.title: Comparison of Regression Models for Predicting Major Primal-Cut Weights across Carcass-Weight Categories in Landrace × Yorkshire × Duroc Pigs
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to identify the best-performing regression algorithm for predicting the weights of major primal cuts within each pig carcass weight category, in order to improve the accuracy of meat yield estimation.Methods: Data from 2,676,916 Landrace × Yorkshire × Duroc (LYD) pigs slaughtered between 2022 and 2024 were utilized.Carcass weights were categorized into five intervals: ≤70, 71-80, 81-90, 91-100, and >100 kg.Five types of regression models (simple linear regression, multiple linear regression, Elastic Net, partial least squares regression, and random forest) were applied to seven primal cuts (shoulder blade, shoulder picnic, loin, belly, ribs, tenderloin, and ham).Model robustness was further assessed via 5-fold cross-validation, nested hyperparameter tuning, external temporal validation, VIFbased multicollinearity screening, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification of R² and RMSE.Results: The SLR models showed low explanatory power with coefficients of determination (R 2 ) ranging from 0.04 to 0.66.In contrast, MLR and Elastic Net demonstrated high predictive performance for most primal cuts and weight intervals, with R 2 values between 0.56 and 0.99.RF exhibited particularly high explanatory power for the belly.Carcass weight was confirmed as the most critical variable across all cuts, showing a strong positive correlation.Lean meat percentage generally had a positive influence on cut weights, whereas fat percentage had a negative influence, except in the belly, where fat-related variables were highly significant.Backfat thickness, sex, and season had limited impact on prediction performance. Conclusion:The results of this study confirmed the differences in primal cut growth patterns by carcass weight categories and demonstrated that advanced regression models can accurately predict yields.This is expected to provide fundamental data for precise yield estimation and the establishment of data driven production strategies, helping to enhance the efficiency of slaughter and meat processing management.

papers.title: Soil phenotyping: Integrating phenosoils and proximal soil sensing for spatiotemporal characterisation of managed soil variability
papers.abstract: The characterisation of soil variability has challenged soil science since the early recognition that soils exhibit complex, structured spatial patterns across landscapes. As agriculture intensifies and soils are expected to deliver more—storing carbon, supporting biodiversity, and sustaining other key functions—there is an urgent need for scalable, quantitative methods to monitor and manage soil variability across space and time. Here we synthesise and advance a framework for soil phenotyping, defined as the quantitative assessment of soil structural, chemical, physical, and biological properties and their spatiotemporal patterns using proximal sensing—explicitly grounded in the distinction between genosoils (baseline soils under minimal human influence) and phenosoils (persistent management-modified soil expressions). Drawing parallels with field plant phenotyping, we argue that soils exhibit phenotypic responses arising from interactions among inherent soil capacity, environmental, and management drivers, and that these responses can be measured efficiently using high-throughput sensing. We review proximal soil sensing technologies, including electromagnetic induction and vis–NIR spectroscopy, and discuss their integration within multi-sensor platforms, digital soil mapping, and machine-learning workflows for data fusion, prediction, and uncertainty quantification. We position soil phenotyping as a practical pipeline from in situ sensing to spatially explicit indicators of soil condition and function, supporting precision agriculture, soil health assessment, and soil security planning. Finally, we identify key challenges for operational deployment, including calibration transferability, sensor harmonisation, spatiotemporal sampling design, and open, interoperable data frameworks, and outline research priorities to accelerate adoption in managed landscapes

papers.title: Evaluating student perceptions of image-based audience response questions in medical education
papers.abstract: Audience response systems have been extensively utilized in medical and pharmacy education to improve learner engagement and knowledge retention. Unlike traditional ARSs that utilize text-based multiple-choice questions Hotspot is an image-based ARS integrated into PointSolutions that allows students to answer questions by selecting areas of interest on images and figures, rather than choosing from multiple-choice options. The purpose of this study was to evaluate student perceptions of integrating Hotspot into pharmacology and biomedical curricula, including perceived engagement, learning reinforcement, usability and preferences relative to traditional MCQs. Faculty at California Northstate University incorporated Hotspot questions into the lectures of first- and second-year courses across three matriculating classes. Following these sessions, students completed an anonymous survey. Survey items assessed student perceptions of engagement, perceived learning, and ease of use on a seven-point Likert scale. Learners reported that Hotspot technology made it easier to pay attention during lectures (median Likert score of six out of seven [interquartile range (IQR) 5–7]; n = 99). They felt the questions were a good use of class time (6 out of 7 [interquartile range 6–7]; n = 99) and indicated that the interactive format challenged them and reinforced their understanding better than MCQs (6 out of 7 [IQR 5–7]; n = 99). Overall, learners expressed a preference for Hotspot over traditional MCQs and reported that this approach was more engaging. These findings support the feasibility and learner acceptability of incorporating image-based active learning strategies and provide evidence to support the adoption of innovative instructional approaches in medical and pharmacology education.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural identification of unmeasurable contact damping in helical hydraulic actuators via spectral-aware hard-gating mechanism
papers.abstract: The helical oscillating cylinder (HOC) is a compact, high-torque-density actuator whose internal contact damping is difficult to measure directly, limiting dynamic-model calibration. We present a model-based identification framework that integrates architectural and training strategies to address high-frequency transient responses, pre-impact causality, and coupled damping-parameter optimization. A four-degree-of-freedom lumped-parameter model describes startup impacts using a modified Hertzian viscoelastic contact law. On this basis, a hard-gating physics-informed neural network (HG-PINN) combines spectral-aware Fourier features, causal hard gating, and freeze–thaw two-phase training. Ablation studies examine how these components and the training strategy contribute to transient-response reconstruction and stable damping-parameter identification. In tests using synthetic acceleration responses with additive Gaussian noise, both damping-parameter errors remained below 1% at 30% noise and below 3% at 50% noise. Against a deterministic Levenberg– Marquardt baseline under identical forward-model settings, HG-PINN retained substantially lower errors as noise increased. It required no external forward-model evaluations during parameter updates. These modelto- model tests support the robustness of HG-PINN under the tested noise conditions and motivate future experimental validation for digital-twin calibration of hydraulic actuators.

papers.title: Solidification‐Derived Intermetallic Architectures in Heat‐Resistant Aluminum Alloys: A Review
papers.abstract: Conventional precipitation‐strengthened aluminum alloys often lose load‐bearing capacity above approximately 300 °C as matrix softening accompanies precipitate coarsening or dissolution. Solidification‐derived intermetallic architectures offer an alternative route to elevated‐temperature strength through thermally stable lamellar, fibrous, cellular, divorced, or three‐dimensional networks. This review examines heat‐resistant aluminum alloys containing eutectic, near‐eutectic, primary‐phase‐plus‐eutectic, and rapidly solidified eutectic‐like architectures. A manufacturing‐process‐aware framework links alloy chemistry, local thermal history, intermetallic architecture, and defect population across casting, laser powder bed fusion, electron beam powder bed fusion, laser directed energy deposition, and wire arc additive manufacturing. Evidence is categorized into phase stability and hardness retention, instantaneous high‐temperature strength, creep and rupture, fatigue, and component‐scale qualification. Cross‐family comparisons show that refined spacing alone does not ensure heat resistance. Sustained performance also requires sufficient phase fraction, stable morphology and connectivity, matrix strength, interfacial integrity, and tolerance to route‐specific defects. Available studies demonstrate condition‐specific capability within parts of the 300–400 °C range, but the evidence remains uneven and often derives from unmatched test conditions. The resulting family–route–condition framework provides transferable reporting descriptors and qualification priorities without equating thermal stability with structural capability under sustained loading.

papers.title: A Biomanufacturing Digital Twin for Consistent N‐1 Seed Bioreactor Transfers for Commercial Monoclonal Antibody Production
papers.abstract: Process consistency in biomanufacturing, particularly for commercial products, is critical for achieving consistent yield and product quality. The N-1 seed bioreactor stage, where cells grow before the transfer to a production bioreactor, often faces variability in final viable cell density (VCD), which leads to variable seeding densities in the production bioreactor and subsequent variability in total protein output per batch. In this study, we address the challenge of precise batch transfer by developing an upstream, stage-specific, level-2 digital twin (digital shadow). Here we show that a cell growth process model predicts growth accurately and updates forecasts using off-line and in-line measurements, enabling precise determination of the final sample time. Deployment of this seed transfer digital twin led to all N-1 to production transfers falling within acceptable limits and resulted in statistically significant increases in harvest yield relative to historical batches. This improvement is attributed to significantly higher on-target accuracy of final N-1 VCDs and significantly higher working volumes in the production bioreactors. Our findings demonstrate that such digital twins ensure consistent cell density during transfer, improve overall upstream process consistency, and lay a foundation for more advanced process control strategies.

papers.title: Revision Hip Arthroscopy Patient Acceptable Symptom State Thresholds at Minimum 5‐Year Follow‐Up Show Imperfect Agreement With Patient Satisfaction
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To report patient acceptable symptom state (PASS) thresholds at a minimum 5-year follow-up after revision hip arthroscopy for the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), Non-Arthritic Hip Score (NAHS), visual analog scale (VAS), and International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (iHOT-12) and to evaluate the agreement between PASS classification and patient-reported satisfaction. METHODS: Prospectively collected data were retrospectively reviewed for all patients who underwent revision hip arthroscopy between 2008 and 2018 for persistent femoroacetabular impingement symptoms. Patients were included in the study if they had preoperative and minimum 5-year postoperative scores for mHHS, NAHS, VAS, and iHOT-12 with anchor questions. Patients were excluded if they had Workers' Compensation claims, osteoarthritis, or conversion to total hip arthroplasty. Thresholds for achieving PASS were determined using receiver-operating characteristic curve analysis. Agreement between PASS classification and patient-reported satisfaction was also evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 94 patients (94 hips) who underwent revision hip arthroscopy met the inclusion criteria, and 60 (64%) completed the satisfaction anchor at minimum 5-year follow-up. Achievement PASS rates were 63.3% for mHHS, 60.0% for NAHS, 75.0% for VAS, and 61.7% for iHOT-12. Area under the curve values from receiver-operating characteristic curves were 0.862 for mHHS, 0.802 for NAHS, 0.873 for VAS, and 0.877 for iHOT-12. PASS values were determined to be 71.0 for mHHS (sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 83.3%), 72.5 for NAHS (76.2%, 77.8%), 4.9 for VAS (95.2%, 72.2%), and 54.7 for iHOT-12 (83.3%, 88.9%). Among patients reporting satisfaction, 18.3% failed to meet at least 1 PASS threshold, whereas 5% of patients exceeded PASS thresholds despite reporting dissatisfaction. CONCLUSIONS: Thresholds for PASS of commonly used PROs were identified at minimum 5-year follow-up after revision hip arthroscopy. However, imperfect agreement between PASS classification and satisfaction was observed. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective case series.

papers.title: Κτηριακό κέλυφος : μελέτη επίδρασης της θερμομόνωσης και της υάλωσης στην ενεργειακή απόδοση κτηριών κατοικίας
papers.abstract: This Diploma Thesis develops a generalized computational framework for the classification and prediction of the impact response of laminated composite plates. The methodology is based on the Impact Characterization Diagram and combines machine learning, multifidelity modelling and active learning. First, a Random Forest classifier is employed to automatically identify the response region as Local, Transition or Global. For the Local and Transition regions, a multifidelity model is developed in which the FSDT-TDSFE formulation is used as the low-fidelity model, while the more detailed CLW-TDSFE formulation provides the high-fidelity response. The discrepancy between the two fidelity levels is approximated through Gaussian Process regression, while Active Learning is employed to adaptively select the most informative high-fidelity simulations, thereby reducing the required computational effort. The final methodology is assessed through independent validation cases in order to examine its ability to predict the response of previously unseen impact conditions. For the Global region, a separate analytical damage dependent formulation is employed, in which delamination is incorporated through the reduction of the effective structural stiffness and represented within the Generalized Impact Characterization Diagram. Overall, the proposed framework combines the physical interpretation of the impact problem with data-driven prediction methods and enables the selection of an appropriate analysis strategy according to the identified impact-response region.

papers.title: Nanotechnology in orthopedic surgery: Advances, applications, and future directions
papers.abstract: Nanotechnology has emerged as a promising platform in orthopedic medicine, offering potential solutions to persistent challenges in implant integration, bone regeneration, cartilage repair, and oncologic drug delivery. This narrative review summarizes recent advancements in orthopedic nanotechnology and critically evaluates their translational readiness. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2010–2026), including peer-reviewed English-language studies on implant surface modification, bone tissue engineering, cartilage and meniscus regeneration, and targeted cancer therapeutics. Most available evidence remains preclinical ( in vitro and animal studies), with limited human clinical data. Nanostructured surfaces have demonstrated improved osteoblast adhesion and early osseointegration in preclinical models. Nanofibrous scaffolds enhance mechanical strength and guide stem-cell differentiation, while stimuli-responsive nanocarriers promote chondrogenesis and support meniscal repair. In orthopedic oncology, functionalized nanocarriers enable passive and active tumor targeting and may overcome multidrug resistance. Future progress will depend on standardized safety guidelines, scalable manufacturing approaches, and the integration of artificial intelligence-driven nanomaterial design an emerging field in which machine-learning models are increasingly used to predict nanoparticle behavior, optimize surface chemistry, and accelerate biomaterial discovery.

papers.title: Meta-Bayesian Fusion Adaptation for Evacuation Prediction: A Hybrid XGBoost–Graph Neural Network Framework for the Mentawai Megathrust Scenario
papers.abstract: Continuous monitoring of physiological conditions in intensive care units generates complex multivariate time-series data that can support early clinical decision-making. However, conventional hybrid models combining Long Short-Term Memory networks and XGBoost generally learn correlational patterns and may experience performance degradation under non-stationary conditions, sensor artifacts, and changes in patient characteristics. Moreover, these models are typically designed for outcome prediction rather than treatment-effect estimation. Therefore, a framework capable of integrating temporal forecasting, representation disentanglement, uncertainty estimation, and treatment-response analysis is required. Purpose: This study aims to develop a Causal Multi-Task Fusion Engine (CMTFE) for forecasting future vital-sign trajectories and estimating individualized treatment effects in IoT-supported ICU monitoring. Methods/Study Design/Approach: The proposed framework integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network for multivariate vital-sign encoding, a β-Variational Autoencoder for separating outcome-relevant and confounding representations, a Transformer decoder for probabilistic trajectory forecasting, and propensity-weighted XGBoost regressors for treatment-effect estimation. Experiments were conducted using 487,000 observation windows derived from 38,200 ICU stays in the MIMIC-IV dataset. The data were chronologically divided into training, validation, and testing sets at proportions of 70%, 15%, and 15%, respectively. Forecasting performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error, and Continuous Ranked Probability Score. Treatment-effect estimation was evaluated on a semi-synthetic test set using Precision in Estimation of Heterogeneous Effect and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve. Results/Findings: CMTFE achieved an MAE of 0.281, RMSE of 0.390, and CRPS of 0.218, outperforming the evaluated LSTM, TCN, Transformer, LSTM–XGBoost, and TCN–XGBoost baselines. Under the constructed distribution-shift scenario, the model exhibited a relative MAE increase of 4.2%, compared with 9.5% for TCN–XGBoost. For semi-synthetic treatment-effect estimation, CMTFE obtained a PEHE of 0.187 and an AUC of 0.842. The ablation analysis further indicated that representation disentanglement, contrastive regularization, propensity-score weighting, and temporal convolution each contributed to the model’s performance. Novelty/Originality/Value: The principal contribution of this study lies in integrating temporal forecasting, disentangled representation learning, uncertainty quantification, and propensity-adjusted treatment-effect estimation within a unified ICU-monitoring framework. Unlike conventional hybrid models that combine neural and tree-based predictions through passive aggregation, CMTFE uses learned outcome-relevant representations to support both forecasting and intervention-response analysis. Nevertheless, the treatment-effect findings are based on semi-synthetic outcomes and should be interpreted as experimental decision-support evidence rather than validated clinical recommendations. External, prospective, and clinician-centered validation is required before real-world deployment.

papers.title: Physically Active Learning and Primary Students' Outcomes: A Bibliometric Science Mapping Study (2000–2026)
papers.abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of Physically Active Learning (PAL) and its relationship with primary school students' learning outcomes. To the best of the authors' knowledge, no prior bibliometric study has exclusively focused on PAL as a pedagogical construct. Using the Scopus database (2000–2026), a modified PRISMA approach, and VOSviewer v.1.6.20, 1,001 articles from 374 journals were analyzed. The dataset yielded 21,897 citations, an h-index of 68, and a CAGR of 17.1% (2010–2025). Three temporal phases were identified: health-oriented foundation (2000–2010), pedagogical diversification (2011–2017), and expansion–consolidation (2018–2026). Thematic analyses suggest a gradual paradigm shift from PAL as a health intervention toward a pedagogically oriented strategy, reflected in the increasing prominence of embodied learning and movement integration. The United States dominates global production (45.1%), while Indonesia remains underrepresented (1.5%). This study proposes research directions for Indonesian scholars, including traditional game-based PAL interventions and Merdeka Belajar curriculum integration. papers.title: An Adaptive Optimization Strategy Applied to the Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
papers.abstract: Balancing exploration and exploitation remains a central challenge in metaheuristic optimization, particularly for engineering applications requiring both global search efficiency and reliable convergence. This paper introduces a simple and adaptive strategy that dynamically adjusts the behavior of an optimization algorithm based on real‑time performance feedback. The method identifies key search operators and assigns each an explorative and exploitative variant, grouped into two optimization modes. An online mechanism switches between these modes according to the successful mutation rate, enabling the optimizer to respond to the evolving landscape of the search process. The strategy is integrated into the artificial bee colony algorithm and evaluated on 18 numerical benchmarks, a CEC2021 test suite, and a nonlinear model predictive control problem. Results demonstrate improved robustness, competitive accuracy, and faster convergence by reducing the number of evaluations by more than 4% against the established GABC, highlighting the method’s suitability for complex industrial optimization

papers.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
papers.abstract: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.

llm.why_not_core: The paper targets EUV lithography post-exposure bake reaction-diffusion, with no FEA structural mechanics, no implant/biomechanics context, and no stress-shielding or contact validation.
