summary_en.motivation: Sequential time marching makes post-exposure bake reaction-diffusion simulation computationally expensive at large three-dimensional scales.
summary_en.method: The coupled acid-quencher equations are recast as nonlinear Volterra integral equations via the Duhamel principle, solved with polynomial temporal bases and Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, and embedded in a physics-informed neural operator.
summary_en.result: The approach simulates a 1200×1200×100 voxel domain within roughly one minute and enables time-marching-free concentration prediction at arbitrary bake times.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through three-dimensional PEB simulation cases comparing the integral solver and its PINO extension.

papers.title: Investigating Deformation and Residual Stress in Overhang Structures Produced by Laser Powder Bed Fusion: An Experimental And Thermo-Mechanical Simulation Study
papers.abstract: In laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), overhang structures are particularly vulnerable to warping and residual stress buildup due to inadequate thermal dissipation and limited mechanical support. While contour scanning is commonly used to improve surface quality, its effects on stress distribution and deformation mechanisms in overhang geometries are not fully understood. This study systematically investigates the impact of contour scanning on overhang components with angles from 45° to 60°, combining experimental tests with coupled thermo-mechanical finite element (FE) simulations. Overhang specimens made of 316L stainless steel were produced using an SLM 125HL system. Experimental results revealed that increasing the overhang angle led to greater deformation, surface defects, and melt-through occurrences. To better understand these behaviors, an FE model incorporating Goldak’s double-ellipsoidal heat source and temperature-dependent material properties was developed to simulate the evolution of temperature and stress during contour scanning. Using a reduced-geometry approach—where the model is scaled down in all dimensions to represent three deposited layers (90 μm) over a 1 mm scan length, with volume hatching excluded—the simulation successfully replicates the qualitative deformation patterns and residual stress accumulation observed in the experiments. The simulation further reveals that localized thermal gradients around contour paths induce asymmetric warping at the free ends of overhangs and generate stress concentrations near constrained regions. These insights emphasize the pivotal role of contour scanning in the formation of deformation and residual stresses and provide valuable guidance for optimizing processing parameters to successfully fabricate unsupported overhang features in L-PBF.

papers.title: A nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F barrier-reservoir coating on 316L stainless steel coordinates anti-infective and osteoregenerative responses.
papers.abstract: Early-stage bacterial infection and inadequate osseointegration remain major causes of failure of orthopedic 316L stainless steel (316L SS) implants. Fluoride-containing surfaces can provide antibacterial activity and support angiogenic and osteoblastic responses when fluoride exposure is appropriately regulated. However, uncontrolled release may cause burst exposure, compromised cytocompatibility, and limited functional durability. Herein, a nanostructured gradient Ta-O-F coating was constructed on 316L SS by stepwise plasma modification: an outer Ta2O5-rich region served as a corrosion-stable barrier, whereas an underlying fluoride-containing region functioned as an ion reservoir, thereby suppressing burst fluoride release and sustaining subsequent exposure. Compared with monofunctional coatings, TO/TF showed improved corrosion resistance, moderated fluoride release, and retained antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli. Phenotypic and transcriptomic analyses indicated that the antibacterial response was primarily associated with fluoride-mediated membrane damage, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbance, and suppression of translation-related pathways. The Ta2O5-rich surface may provide an additional but relatively weak contribution through corrosion stabilization and favorable surface physicochemical properties. The regulated coating also enhanced endothelial migration and tube formation, while promoting osteoblastic adhesion, proliferation, ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and related gene expression in vitro. In an infected rat implantation model, TO/TF reduced local inflammatory infiltration and bacterial burden relative to unmodified 316L SS, while supporting vascular and osteogenic marker expression and improved peri-implant bone architecture. These findings establish a barrier-reservoir strategy for coordinating early anti-infective protection with subsequent osteoregenerative responses on metallic implants.
